articles.title: How to Read the Dune Books in Chronological Order
articles.summary: The Dune series is currently at an astounding 23 novels and counting; spanning 15,000 years. If you're wondering where to start, we're here to help.
articles.body:
Ever since Frank Herbert released his seminal sci-fi novel Dune in 1965, readers have been consumed by the expansive and complex political wranglings of his influential stories. While Herbert only wrote six Dune novels while he was alive, since his death, his son Brian Herbert and bestselling author Kevin J. Anderson have authored many new canon Dune stories. In fact, the series is currently at an astounding 23 novels and counting; spanning 15,000 years. If you're wondering where to start and how you're supposed to read them, we're here to help.

With the most recent Dune: Part 3 trailer hyping the third film in the franchise, now is the perfect time to dive into the novels that started it all. Below we've detailed out the entire Dune book timeline for your convenience. Reading all of the Dune books in order can be a bit tricky depending on where you start.

There are technically a total of 23 Dune Books in the franchise , but there are only 6 novels officially written by Frank Herbert himself . All of the books listed below are technically canon, and fit somewhere in the Dune timeline, but many of them have been written by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson.

Includes 6 Books Frank Herbert Dune Box Set

All Dune Books: Chronological Reading Order

Warning: Each of the blurbs in this piece contains spoilers for the Dune book series.

1. The Butlerian Jihad by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

The Butlerian Jihad by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Despite being written decades after the original Dune, Herbert and Anderson use this prequel — the first in a trilogy — to establish and expand on much of the world building and lore from the original. Chronologically this novel takes place earliest in the Dune canon around 10,000 years before the events of Herbert's original novel. Setting up the feudal and technologically-barren world of the books, this story follows the beginnings of a brutal world-changing war between the last free humans and the artificial intelligence and robotics they created.

2. The Machine Crusade by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

The Machine Crusade by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

In the second book in Herbert and Anderson's trilogy, readers get to meet more vital players in the wider world of Dune. As the war rages on, readers spend time with ancestors of House Atreides and House Harkonnen while the humans continue their battle with the evil sentient computer overlord Ominus. Dense worldbuilding and intricate plotting fill the pages of this book which builds on what's come before while setting the stage for an epic final battle.

3. The Battle of Corrin by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Set 100 years after the events at the beginning of The Butlerian Jihad, the book finds Ominus' plan for universal domination moving ever closer to success. As the most gruesome era of the war begins, history is made. Ominus' dangerous games push the universe to breaking point as each planet does what it must to survive. Establishing much of the status quo of the original book, this entry vitally introduces the battle ready iteration of the Fremen Paul meets in Dune.

4. Sisterhood of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

The next chronological step in Herbert and Anderson's trilogies is the "Schools of Dune." After another large time jump—this time 83 years—the story focuses on a burgeoning world without the so-called "thinking machines" and how that impacts the universe. Following disparate characters as they venture around the galaxy, there are important reveals about the growing Butlerian movement, and the dangerous violence that's thrumming across the universe.

5. Mentats of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

With the thinking machines all but destroyed a school is established to train "Mentats" humans of supreme intelligence who can essentially replace the machines the war demolished. Other academies are being founded too including a new school of the sisterhood on Wallach IX. But within their ranks is a young woman desperate for vengeance who could bring down everything. As the schools battle for survival, so does the universe as the Butlerian fanatics rise.

6. Navigators of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Continuing the origin of the Bene Gesserit, Mentat and Suk Schools, this final book in this trilogy focuses on the ever-growing threat of the anti-technology forces who were inspired by the Butlerian Jihad. Can reason win out against the ever growing fanaticism spreading across the universe? That's the big question as Herbert and Anderson build on this growing chasm.

7. House Atreides by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Finally gaining on the original Dune novels, the first book in the Prelude to Dune trilogy takes place just 35 years before they begin. Complex threads come together as we get introductions to some major players like Leto Atredis, Duncan Idaho, Baron Harkonnen, and the Reverend Mother Gaius Helen Mohiam. Political shenanigans are at a high here as games are played, loyalty is sought, and the stage is set for an epic battle that will change the universe.

8. House Harkonnen by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Continuing the Prelude trilogy this novel continues to establish the drama and scheming that lays the groundwork for the original Dune novels. As Houses Harkonnen and Atredis struggle for power, the Bene Gesserit begin to plot towards their ultimate aim: creating the chosen one known as the Kwisatz Haderach, by introducing Leto to his concubine Jessica. So if you've always wanted to know what led to the events of Herbert's beloved books, here's your answer.

9. House Corrino by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Topping off the Prelude trilogy is this action-packed novel that centers around Leto, Jessica, and their soon to be born son Paul. As the parents eagerly await their new arrival, the witches of the Bene Gesserit couldn't be more excited as they know their chosen one is on the way. But if you've read the Dune books you'll know they might be less than happy with the result.

10. Princess of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Telling the stories of the two women in Paul Atreides' life, this companion novel focuses on the wife he was forced to marry, Irulan, and the woman he fell in love with on his adventures, Chani. Their dueling stories drive forward this book that gives an expansive look at the women around Paul and how their lives and experiences led them to him for better or for worse.

11. The Duke of Caladan by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

The final new trilogy before we reach Herbert's first Dune novel, the Caldan stories center around Paul's father Leto Atreides and his rise to power in the universe. Through honesty, action, and integrity, Duke Leto finds himself with ever more power and status in the political center of the galaxy, but his new status sets him on a dangerous and ultimately fatal course.

12. The Lady of Caladan by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

When Lady Jessica betrayed the Bene Gesserit her life was changed forever, in this book we see how that choice and its fallout changed the shape of the universe. When pitted against the ancient order how can one woman — and her love for her family — ever win? And what lengths will she have to go in order to make the ultimate choice and more pressingly to survive?

13. The Heir of Caladan by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

As this trilogy comes to an end it centers on the rise of Paul Atriedes better known to the universe as Muad’Dib. But he has yet to take on that title here and instead must go on a journey to find himself and the strength to lead. If you've made it this far then you're about to be rewarded by reading the original novel that started it all...

The book that sparked it all, Herbert's soft sci-fi introduced readers to House Atreides and their young son Pual as they embark on a quest to control and run the wealthy Spice trade on the arid planet Arrakis. Focusing on the interplanetary politics and expansive planetary landscape of his world, Dune is an exceptionally dense read but it's essential to understand the scope of Herbert's creation. While it was obviously the first published Dune book, since Herbert and Anderson's many prequels, it now hits somewhere in the middle of the reading list.

15. Paul of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Acting as both a prequel and sequel to Dune, this story follows Paul Atreidis before and after the events of the book. As a young child he's entangled in the dangerous politics of the universe as they prepare for his father's wedding. When we join him after Dune we learn more about his time with the Fremen and his relationship with his lover Chani as the pair build a life together.

Speaking of Paul Atreidis, he's at the center of Herbert's second book where we join him a decade after becoming Emperor. After taking on the mantle of Messiah to the Fremen Paul has unintentionally inspired another universal Jihad, creating havoc and war across galaxies. Thanks to his visions Paul hopes to change the dire future he's created but it won't be easy.

17. The Winds of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

With Paul lost in the deserts and thought to be dead this book builds in the time between Dune Messiah and Children of Dune. Catching up with Paul's mother Jessica, her daughter and Emperor Regent Alia, and Duncan Idaho, this is a galaxy spanning adventure that adds context and history to the original writings of Herbert while introducing important lore and worldbuilding.

As the ecological landscape of Arrakis changes drastically so does the shape of the universe. Paul of Atreidis young children Leto and Ghanima deal with his legacy in Herbert's third book as they battle against their fates and wonder whether they'll end up just like their dad. The Spice trade comes under threat from an unexpected source and a new leader emerges.

After the shocking events of the last book we join Leto 3500 years later. How is he almost 4000 years old? Well he merged with a Sandworm in Children of Dune and has since been ruling the universe with an iron fist and brutal regime. This novel follows Leto and inspects his impact on the cosmos as he attempts to keep his rule and hold on the Spice trade no matter what.

Get ready for another time jump! This time we're visiting Arrakis 1500 years after the death of God Emperor Leto. Humanity is burgeoning once again and Sandworms have made a resurgence. Three new civilisations reign, including the Bene Gesserit who are struck with a near impossible choice: keep their behind the scenes role as master manipulators of the universe or become true leaders to make the most of the power vacuum in the universe.

Finding themselves in a brutal battle with another Matriarchal organization, the Honored Matres, the Bene Gesserit become entangled in a war for survival against their violent foes. This was Herbert's final book and ends on a famous cliffhanger which he was never able to resolve as he died after its publication. But his son and collaborator Anderson would later continue the story.

22. Hunters of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

The first of a duology that adapts notes left by Herbert for what was planned for Dune 7. Continuing the story from Herbert's books this title explores the fallout from the war between the Bene Gesserit and the Honored Matres, as well as the return of the many, many descendants of the humans who were scattered across the universe during the reign of God Emperor Leto.

23. Sandworms of Dune by Brian Herbert and Kevin J. Anderson

Filled with clones, shocking returns, and a huge reveal about the antagonists of the series, this is an event level book that brings together the many loose threads left by the original books. Combining a complex structure, multiple character arcs, and an epic final battle this is a true climax to the overarching Dune series, which has been evolving and growing since 1967.

It's possible Brian Herbert writes more Dune books, but the massive success of the Dune and Dune Part 2 movies means we'll certainly be seeing more of the series on screen. The next movie in the series, Dune: Part 3 is set to release on December 18, 2026. The most recent trailer showcased how it adapts Frank Herbert's second book: Dune Messiah.

In case you missed it, there's also a new video game based on Dune. Funcom is currently developing an open world survival MMO called Dune: Awakening .

Rosie Knight is a contributing freelancer for IGN covering everything from anime to comic books to kaiju to kids movies to horror flicks. She has over half a decade of experience in entertainment journalism with bylines at Nerdist, Den of Geek, Polygon, and more.

articles.title: Sony is killing all physical PlayStation game discs
articles.summary: ﻿New games released after January 2028 will be digital-only.
articles.body: Sony has announced that from January 2028 it will entirely stop the production of physical discs for new PlayStation games. From that point onwards, new releases will only be available in digital versions from the PlayStation Store and other retailers. Games released before January 2028 will still be available on disc. “This is a natural direction for Sony Interactive Entertainment to adapt to consumer trends as the general preference for digital media significantly outpaces physical discs,” Sony said in its announcement. “This transition will enable us to align more closely with how most of our community prefers to access and play games today.” The move follows the recent announcement that Grand Theft Auto VI’s physical edition will only be a download code in a box, which prompted a quick backlash from fans. While digital copies of games have some obvious advantages, they deny buyers any resale value, make it harder to share games, and leave players reliant on ongoing access to console servers and accounts to access their games.

articles.title: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 Spices Up Anime Fighters With the Soul Switching Mechanic | IGN Preview
articles.summary: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3's bigger focus on multiplayer PvE seems like the right direction for Xenoverse. Not just because it would be tough to top Xenoverse 2 as one of the shining examples of the Anime Fighter genre and live service games in general, but as a potential tone-setter for the genre going forward.
articles.body:
Xenoverse 3 leans into the near-fact that most players want to play as their favorite character.

Raid gameplay combats the monotony and predictability in many other arena fighters.

I think fans of series like Dragon Ball are probably tired of the same old anime fighter – I know I am. If you’ve booted one up, you’ve probably experienced their repetitive formula that hasn’t meaningfully changed in well over a decade. As fun as it is to remember an iconic standoff, I think I’d rather just rewatch it (or a fan edit) instead of hammering away at the same button for a few minutes. And from a distance, I’d forgive anime fans for thinking that Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 is just another mashy arena fighter caked in glitzy fan service.

Instead, a beefy demo hosted at Bandai Namco headquarters in Tokyo reminded me that developer Dimps is among the best at making these. The demo session focused exclusively on co-op multiplayer, with no mention of the arena fighter mode. Focused on fun and fan service, this game’s seemingly sprawling lobbies and chill, raid-style co-op levels indicate a ton of potential as a digital third space. Some of the more repetitive aspects you’ll find in a lot of anime brawlers are still there, it’s true, but Xenoverse 3 handles them better than most, twisting and expanding them around raids. And to fight that staleness even more, Dimps brings a dizzying amount of customization to the toy chest that they’re stocking with anything a fan could ask for.

Set in Age 1000, many of the series’ most iconic heroes and villains are long gone, leaving room for you to forge your own story in Xenoverse 3’s seemingly deep RPG-like progression. They’ll still show up in their own way – after all, what’s a Dragon Ball game without Goku and Vegeta – but this isn’t the era most fans will know. Brought to life using leftover documents from late Dragon Ball artist and creator Akira Toriyama, Xenoverse 3 is a pillar of the brand’s push into this new era. That will show in its story, which Bandai Namco claims is the longest in the series’ history, but also in the art.

This setting lightens Xenoverse 3’s load in following up 2, which stands in rarified air. Thanks to years of support and a dedicated player base, this setting removes 3 from needing to directly follow up 2, which is still surprisingly current considering its age. That’s also given its strong player community a good reason to keep it alive for nearly 10 years. Age 1000 feels like a convenient tonal and artistic zag, letting the longtime DBX team help establish this new era in the wake of Akira Toriyama’s passing. That said, my demo and subsequent group interview mostly focused on multiplayer. If you’d like to hear more about Age 1000, Xenoverse 3’s solo content, and the protagonist’s messy room, we went hands-on back in June and had an extended interview with the team.

Like that last demo, mine started with a choice between four races: Human, Saiyan, Namekian, and Frieza – two more than last time. I opted for the Namekian on my first run through a raid; an homage to The Dad Who Stepped Up, Piccolo. After picking my character and loading into the infamous messy room from our last article (didn’t seem that bad to me), representatives from Bandai Namco shuttled us into the main multiplayer lobby. They were pretty careful about getting us to where we needed to go, so I didn’t get a good look at everything going on behind the scenes of the multiplayer. But what little I saw seemed pretty big for a simple lobby.

This makes sense; Xenoverse 2 was ahead of the curve with its online suite. If you’ve played a fighting game in the last few years, you’ve certainly seen its influence. Turning a multiplayer menu into a navigable hub world changed how people played fighting games online. From VR Chat to Fortnite, these digital third spaces have become even more important to and celebrated by online communities since that big swing 10 years ago. It’s a clever bet on the Xenoverse player community that’s sure to pay off in spades if it’s taken.

Once everyone from my group session had assembled in the notably smaller pregame lobby area, I stopped flying around the room and got ready for the first battle. Before hitting that ready-up button, I snooped around the customization menus, choosing a pre-baked costume to ensure an all-around, special-heavy play style, powering up my ranged attacks and special moves without skimping on the other important stuff. The session was relatively short, so I didn’t have enough time to play dress-up, but it seems like you’ll be able to chase function and form in equal measure in the final game. From there, we jumped into the first fight: 50-Foe Fracas.

As advertised, this punch-em-all-till-they’re-dead, 50-enemy fight was pretty straightforward. That horde-style battle fits Xenoverse’s somewhat simple combat system like a glove. Just like the last few games, this execution of the Dragon Ball power fantasy brings the right balance of oomph and speed to each punch, dash, and beam. Xenoverse 3 seems like it’s leaning even more into that power fantasy than ever before with the Soul Switch system.

Whaling on bad guys fills up a special meter, which lets you channel the souls of legendary characters from across the Dragon Ball multiverse. Before I knew it, I was no longer a pre-baked Namekian. Instead, I assumed the form of the master martial artist, Tien, for 40 seconds. My new form came with his moveset and animations, helping me make light work of the Ginyu Force. In my notes, all I wrote was, “Soul Switch kicks ass.”

That Soul Switch mechanic comes with a handful of RPG-like elements, too, emphasizing the bond between your player character and the equipped soul. Dimps is working from the savvy assumption that players will probably always choose their favorite characters in a game like this. So rather than incentivizing swapping around for a specific matchup, it seems like you’ll be rewarded with new branches on a skill tree and some new voice lines for putting your eggs in one basket.

During a group Q&A after the demo, Series Producer Masayuki Hirano also pointed out that this is one of the ways he and his team are addressing the bloat that sometimes plagues these kinds of games, telling us, “There might be a lot of Gokus, but they’ll have different battle styles and movesets, which I think will give the player lots of options to play with” before adding that movesets and skill trees will also come with their own voice lines. He continued, promising, “There is something satisfying about creating that mentorship bond with different versions of characters.”

Before my second mission, I had a little more time to customize my character. This time, I changed into a glass cannon build, and changed my Mentor to Jiren. You can even customize your character’s fighting animations and fighting style, so I swapped mine to Jiren’s. These changes don’t have a meaningful impact on any mechanical difference for your created character or their stats, but it sure is cool!

The next battle saw my squad defending a pair of communication arrays in Communication is Key. This title was ironic, considering the potential issues it brought up. Coming from a more traditional multiplayer mindset, putting defensive objectives in a game that encourages an aggressive playstyle and almost requires everyone to act the hero gave me pause. No matter the genre, from Rematch to Overwatch to League of Legends, nothing kills the vibe like a teammate who won’t play the objective. I didn’t notice anything resembling a ping system (not that it would matter against a hardcore heroballer), which makes me even more concerned.

But again Hirano and co showed me just how well they know their players and the genre, telling me, “We believe Dragon Ball fans all want to charge in there and punch guys, so we want[ed] to make sure that the game was balanced and tuned to be able to do that.” He later added that groups of friends can still design their team around efficiently tackling a specific mission, but reiterated their commitment to letting players “charge in headfirst and punch guys.”

The first two missions I played definitely fit that bill; the intergalactic jobbers we squared off against were no match for my squad, especially thanks to my good pals Tien and Jiren, but the third mission we played was no walk in the park. By far the biggest chunk of the demo, this section resembled a mini dungeon (still a simple one), inside an underground lab. This time, a series of smaller, connecting areas gated by doors that only open once the room is cleared revealed new enemies. It also housed some kind of boss-lite characters that really put up a fight compared to the other two excursions. Ultimately, changing my race to a Frieza didn’t get me where I needed to go. Not even Soul Switching to Majin Buu saved us (though I am pleased to say that I was the last one standing in my group).

I didn’t have time to get another crack at that last lever, but I still got a good feel for the multiplayer side of Xenoverse 3. This bigger focus on multiplayer PvE seems like the right direction for Xenoverse. Not just because it would be tough to top Xenoverse 2 as one of the shining examples of the Anime Fighter genre and live service games in general, but as a potential tone-setter for the genre going forward.

While you're here, check out these recent previews of other big upcoming games we've checked out recently!

Charlie is a freelance contributor for IGN. You can reach them via Twitter or Instagram at the handle @chas_mke.

articles.title: How Being Outsiders Fueled Stranger Than Heaven's Director and Actor to Craft Its Story
articles.summary: Director Mikinobu Abe and lead actor Yu Shirota see Stranger Than Heaven as a more personal story about being an outcast in your own culture.
articles.body:
A story about a half-Japanese man struggling to find his place in the world – I feel particularly suited for covering RGG Studio's upcoming narrative-driven action game Stranger Than Heaven. After playing a new three-hour demo, I had a conversation with the director Mikinobu Abe and lead actor Yu Shirota, who plays the protagonist Makoto Daito, and was able to connect with them on what it meant to create a story about growing up and growing old as an outsider within your own culture.

Abe himself lived abroad and had to learn Japanese when coming back, and Shirota is of mixed heritage, which played a significant role in his career trajectory in acting and music. All of this informed Stranger Than Heaven, alongside the idea that music can break barriers, and that manifests as one of RGG Studio's most intricate in-game side activities yet. And while there are some curious decisions about casting for its characters (see, the digital resurrection of Tupac), having the J-pop idol Ado act and sing for this game is fascinating on its own – I got to the bottom of how that collaboration came together.

Below is our full conversation about all that and more, which has been edited for clarity and readability. For more on the gameplay experience, be sure to read my Stranger Than Heaven extended hands-on preview or watch the video version below.

IGN: The thing that stood out to me most was the theme of music being a core part of gameplay, story, and characters. Walk me through how the idea came to fruition as a consistent theme throughout Stranger Than Heaven.

Mikinobu Abe : We were writing the narrative for this game and thinking of how we should portray Makoto – his life starts at escaping from America and coming to Japan thinking it was heaven, and then it wasn't. And for him, he doesn't have a way to communicate with people because they instantly hate him based on his looks, language, and culture. He realizes that music could be the only thing where he can get treated fairly. Like, good music is good music, no matter what background you come from. And so, how could we realize that? We thought that could be an essential part of Makoto's life, finding something that he can fight fairly in.

That's the starting point, then after that it became related to the Showbiz mechanics where a musical component could be a part of his survival strategy in this harsh environment. And so yeah, that's basically the start of everything. Once we knew we wanted to tell that story, we had Shirota-san with a background in music, and with his background being half-Spanish and half-Japanese, I think those things really clicked together for telling this narrative. The music component is purely of the narrative we wanted to tell.

Yu Shirota : When Mr. [Masayoshi] Yokoyama came to me and told me about this game, he, of course, mentioned the musical part, so I was really interested to listen to his idea. And I thought, that's really interesting with music being a core of the game, and as [Abe-san] said, I have been singing my whole life, more than 25 years. Musicals, singing, and composing. So, I thought that's a perfect role for me. And Mr. Yokoyama also thought that it was the perfect role for me, being half-Spanish and Japanese, feeling like an outsider or a foreigner. But also having hope through music. This role is really, really interesting and also I thought this is the one for me.

IGN: On the topic of music, RGG have had Takaya Kuroda singing karaoke songs in the Yakuza games. So, this feels like a larger extension of that because also the minigames you have here with the band setup and management side activity. Take me through the creation of the Showbiz minigame and why it was important to evolve what we've seen in previous RGG games.

Abe : We never thought of this as a sort of extension of what we have created in the studio's past. Karaoke is karaoke and our minigames in general, including Showbiz, are there to depict the era and the city that we want to depict in each game. So, for the Yakuza and Like A Dragon series, the core concept was to make the player feel like they're in this modern city. For example, when I'm in the 2000s in real-life Tokyo, it has so much variety in what to do within that city. And, of course, karaoke is one of them, right? So all the minigames are based on activities you can do in Tokyo.

That being said, everything's reset in Stranger Than Heaven. We were thinking of resetting it to the point where, okay, we're telling a story in 1915 Kokura then 1929 Kure – what could be something that Makoto can continuously do as a way of survival, but also in a game? What could be something that a player can stick around and do throughout because he'll be like 50 years old. And then Showbiz was one of the core concepts we came up with. It came up when we had this idea of depicting the start of the Yakuza organization. And partially, it's not historically accurate in the game, but the Japanese music industry had some history not just with music, but also with show business in general, and had a few connections. Historically speaking, that's something we can get inspiration from and then make it into the game. It's something Makoto can do within his 50 years of life. So that's how it all began.

And the theme is music being the only way Makoto can basically make a living for himself. When that clicked together, it became this Showbiz mechanic that's in the game now. To add to that, when we were creating this, we started by thinking, what does a promoter do? Because it's not like you're the singer. If you're the singer, we could just make it into a rhythm game. We did have a moment thinking maybe it's a rhythm game? It didn't come up as wanting Makoto to be a promoter, so we started researching what promoters used to do. We'd read hundreds of books figuring out what they used to do. We found out that basically he does everything, from promotion to casting to booking the venue and everything. We thought putting that in the game would be cool, and that's just how it all became the minigame.

IGN: In the minigame, you are the producer of the show, you call when the lights go on and when the smoke and effects happen. I thought that was a cool way to turn it into a little bit of a rhythm game in that sense. [To Yu Shirota] Do you sing in this game? And what was that like?

Shirota : Yes! And that was a lot of fun. There's a scene where I'm following Orpheus, who's Snoop Dogg's character. He teaches [Makoto] how to rap and sing. I actually had a scene where I had to be like Orpheus and that was really hard! But that was a really good experience, trying to rap like Snoop Dogg. Like, here's an American guy who's my friend teaching me, and I don't know how much time I spent recording the scene, but it was really hard and also really fun. And there's more with some scenes of singing like it's a musical and I can't wait to watch it because I haven't seen them yet. I haven't seen it come together, but I put every skill that I have into them.

IGN: That must be crazy since it plays into a lot of things you've done with theater, acting, singing, and that seems really cool, man. And then the reason why Stranger That Heaven is hitting a note with me is because this character is mixed; he's half-Japanese, half-American. And that's something that relates to you, too. For me being half-Filipino, half-American, it's kind of like that identity crisis we go through. When I saw what this game was about, I was thinking, they're making a game about us! To you, why was that an important story to tell?

Abe : For the starting point, while we were making the Yakuza or Like A Dragon series, we were always curious as to who would create such an organization like the yakuza, and also why? That was always back in our heads. We were starting off by thinking, let's just create a game where a man just starts the organization. But we felt like that's a little bit… not boring, but it's just normal. Then we thought, how can we turn this into a narrative that really resonates with people? And then we came up with this idea of having a main character being of mixed heritage of some kind, and that's how we came to a Japanese and American character.

I used to live abroad as well, so I kind of knew the experience. I mean, I wasn't treated like I was of half heritage, but I knew the feeling of coming back to Japan, and I couldn't speak Japanese at the time. Once this concept [for the game] came to life, I was excited at the idea as well. We feel like this theme can really resonate with people, and it also resonates with the development team, including myself, for telling this narrative of Makoto's 50-year journey. It was something really important to us.

IGN: Playing this kind of character, what does that mean to you? How did that feel?

Shirota : When I started my career, it was really hard, especially in Japan. What a producer and director told me was, 'It's tough to find someone like you, but we can't hire you as this character because you're not normal.' That was the most heartbreaking moment for me and I was crying going back to my place! Thinking about that and now in this generation, I think people of half-heritage or someone who has few different cultures, there are so many people like you and me. Not even just nationality, but also sexuality, everything. I think now is good timing and a moment to be like, just be you. Makoto Daito, I think he's going to give people courage or some energy to live in this world, and the message that you don't have to prove anything, and you can just be you.

For me, even though I'm half Spanish, but in a role, I usually play a role where I have a Japanese name every time in Japan. When I do some musicals, it's usually from overseas, especially from America, but in Japan, when I do a movie or TV show, I always have a Japanese name and play a Japanese guy. And even in this game, I'm Makoto Daito, a Japanese name but he's half-American, half-Japanese, and that was really comfortable for me. Because, yeah, that's me. And I hope from now on, I can play these kinds of roles. I'm really glad and happy to have this role in this game and it's one where I could act within this role, for sure.

Stranger Than Heaven Xbox Presents Showcase Images

IGN: This is also a star-studded cast, too. Not just Snoop Dogg, but also Tori Kelly who is well-known. And for me, I'm a huge fan of Ado. She's amazing and one of my favorite singers. Can you tell me what it was like to get her on board for Stranger Than Heaven?

Abe : Getting her on board, hmm. She was really happy to join for the part. We explained the story and we asked her to participate with the role, and there was no challenge there. I mean, no challenge if you ask me, but she really was happy with the role. But one of the harder parts of portraying her as a character was how we should visualize this character who is going to be portrayed by you, Ado? Of course, we don't know her face. So, we worked really closely with her and her agency to nail the character model. We based it off of a face model, one that's obviously not her, and while we were doing all the concept art and 3D models for the character, we really, really worked close with her on how she wanted to look in the game. That was a process that was really fun and it really required our creativity on how we can represent someone who we don't know or her face, yet we've got to make it into a photorealistic character for her. That was fun and challenging while we were developing the game.

IGN: With a lot of names and actors, I'm sure you were excited to work with some of them. What was that like? Did you pick up on anything, work directly with them, or have conversations with them?

Shirota : Unfortunately, I was always alone in a booth so we couldn't do any collaboration when we recorded it. But I saw Dean [Fujioka], who plays Yu Shinjo, and we talked about this game, and I was like, finally I could see them! Because every time when we were recording, I was imagining Snoop Dogg or what it would be like if we were talking to Ado, and I don't know her actual face

Abe : And it was her first time acting, so we didn't know how she would act in a game way, right?

Shirota : So, I really needed some imagination to play this role.

IGN: I can imagine it's very different from being on stage or being on a set, right?

IGN: When you put out the clip of Ado's character talking in a cutscene for the first time, the whole fandom was like, holy s**t??

Shirota : Like, oh, is that her?! I mean, I believe that's her!

Abe : She did an amazing job with acting as Keiko, the character. There are so many good clips that I just really want to share and I can't wait for people to see that in the game.

Shirota : It's really hard to describe, but after listening to her acting voice, I really think that it sounds very Japanese from the Showa era, like a lady from the Showa era in a very classic sounding way.

Abe : Oh my god, this is going to be so hard to explain! There is this certain way of acting that we had back in the era of Showa that actresses used to do. And it really sounds like that style of acting, which really gives this sense of nostalgia to each scene.

Shirota : Even in America or the Philippines, you know, people change the way they speak, right? So I could feel something in her acting that is from Showa, like 40 or 50 years ago.

IGN: You previously mentioned how much research you did for creating these places for the game. I know you said they're not 100% historically accurate and you had creative freedom to create places that do exist, but your own version for the game. And I know this game isn't necessarily about the history of Japan through the 20th century, but I do think it's a very important context for Makoto Daito and his trajectory. What can you tell me about the ways in which you have incorporated the historical element and how things changed in Japan? How is that reflected in Stranger Than Heaven?

Abe : At the end of the day, what was important for us was how we can depict this specific narrative for the game. That was the most important part for deciding the cities and locations in the first place. After doing all the research, we found out so many things that we didn't even know about Japan, and so we took a lot of inspiration from those elements and tried to make sure that we depicted them in the right way. It's been fun and it doesn't have to be entirely accurate, but as long as it's fun as a game or entertaining when we were going through approvals.

You know, I'm sure in 1915, Kokura wasn't like that back then. I'm sure of it. But what was important to us is that the player can feel like this might be realistic for what it could have been like back then. So, not just the research about historical events or what things they were using at the time, but research on the art styles people were using; like, the vintage lens that a photographer used to use back then. We did a lot of research on that kind of stuff and the creators back in those days who we don't even know the names of, yet they left these amazing black and white photos from those days. We did a lot of research on where their inspirations came from so we could depict their creativity in the game, then make players feel like this era and this city actually exists. Especially when doing research on vintage lenses and the film they used, that really helped us shape the world, do color grading for the game, and the cinematography for the cutscenes.

Also, our art director Daishi Kanaya has a background in oil painting. He did a lot of research on what type of painting they used back then and we got inspired by that. Like, if we went back in time, how would we depict those ideas? So, we were trying to reflect that kind of art in the imagination of 2026, but using the equipment that they were using then while trying out different color palettes to fit each era. Everything was to make places believable with some creative freedom and to make the player feel like they are in a specific era in an instant. I think creating vibes out of our research really helped us shape what we have in the game now.

Shirota : The 50 years that span in Stranger Than Heaven, and what's contained within those 50 years? It's not just the time that passes, but also the characters and the relationships between them. Also, you can see them change along with the cities over time. And, like, how entertainment is depicted from the older days where you don't have communication over distances or TVs, and people keep making more direct efforts instead of seeing entertainment from farther away. You could sort of see the start of Japanese entertainment and then see it evolve over that time. Also, you can see Makoto Daito growing as a person, and I feel that those puzzle pieces really fit together to create something beautiful. So that is something I would really like players to experience and appreciate when they do play the game.

Michael is reviews editor at IGN and regularly contributes with previews, interviews, live events coverage, and news all in written and video form. He's usually entrusted with covering long RPGs and tech products, but he's got range when it comes to games. You'll also catch him at conventions and hosting video content, including IGN's weekly podcast Unlocked .

articles.title: “Karl Saw That Her Potential Isn’t Only In The Paint” – WNBA Fans Erupt As Angel Reese Hones 3-Pt Shot Amid Shooting Breakthrough

articles.body:
Angel Reese has been nothing short of legendary in the 2026 WNBA Finals, as the Atlanta Dream leads the series 2-1. The Golden State Valkyries were the best defensive team this season, led by talented players like Gabby Williams. However, Reese has overpowered everyone so far, and her practice routine has now taken the internet by storm.

Reese led the team to a Game 3 win in Atlanta in front of the home crowd, scoring 21 points and grabbing 12 rebounds in 34 minutes. Moreover, her 3-point shooting, which drew heavy criticism during the regular season, has improved. She shot 2-for-2 from deep and garnered praise from veterans.

Meanwhile, the Dream player was seen practicing her long-range shots before Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.

Meanwhile, fans were impressed with Reese's workout, as one pointed out Dream head coach Karl Smesko's impact on her form:

"I'm so happy Karl saw that her potential isn't only in the paint🥹," one fan wrote.

Reese is averaging 21.7 points, 13.3 rebounds, 2.0 assists, 2.0 steals, and 1.0 block per game in the final series. Her impact on both ends of the floor has been great, and she has put forward a strong case for the Finals MVP title.

Angel Reese reveals her mental game against the Valkyries

Angel Reese is one of the most intense players on the court, often through trash talk and mind games. The Finals have also featured intense, competitive moments involving the 2026 Defensive Player of the Year.

In a conversation with the media, Reese shared her secret to success in the ongoing series:

"You can see it in their emotions and facial expressions. A lot of us are looking at that, making sure we can find any little thing to give us that edge and have our leverage over them."

Angel Reese and the Dream are in a strong spot in the series and just a couple of games away from the title. Game 4 tips off Saturday as fans await who picks up the championship this season.

articles.title: Brewers hold on for 3-2 win over Rays in Game 1
articles.summary: It isn’t often that we are treated to a World Series matchup featuring the two best teams in the league. The Brewers won an NL-best 103 games during the regu...
articles.body:
It isn't often that we are treated to a World Series matchup featuring the two best teams in the league. The Brewers won an NL-best 103 games during the regular season while the Rays paced the AL with 98. The matchup lived up to its billing in Game 1 with a thrilling finish.

Milwaukee carried a 3-1 lead into the ninth with closer Trevor Megill on the mound. Milwaukee's relievers entered the series with a 1.33 ERA in 40 2/3 postseason innings. Megill got Yandy Diaz to ground out to start the frame but then allowed back-to-back singles to Jonathan Aranda and Chandler Simpson. With Junior Caminero representing the go-ahead run at the plate, the Rays stayed aggressive and pulled off a double steal to put the tying runs into scoring position.

Megill walked Caminero to load the bases to bring up Liam Hicks and that is when things got interesting. Hicks grounded the first pitch he saw into what appeared to be a game-ending double play. However, the Rays challenged and the replay showed that shortstop Cooper Pratt's foot was off the bag at second when he received the throw from Brice Turang.

Pinch runner Jorge Mateo scored on the play to cut the lead to 3-2. Having thought the game was over, Megill had to come back out with the tying run at third but struck out Jonny DeLuca with a nasty curveball to seal the win.

Catcher William Contreras played a big part in the win for the Brewers. He followed Christian Yelich's RBI triple with a 108 mph single off of shortstop Taylor Walls' glove to stake the Brewers to a 2-0 lead in the first inning.

He also had an impact behind the plate. With the Brewers leading 2-1 in the fifth, Contreras gunned down Victor Mesa Jr. who was trying to steal third with a perfect throw to end the inning.

He also threw out Aranda in the sixth on a failed hit-and-run attempt that ended another threat. Contreras finished the game with two hits, a walk and was also successful on two ABS challenges rounding out an all-around effort.

Jacob Misiorowski got the start for the Brewers on the mound and needed just one pitch to set a World Series record. His 103.5 mph fastball to Diaz to start the game was the fastest recorded pitch in World Series history dating back to 2008 when pitch tracking began.

It wasn't Misiorowski's sharpest performance, but he did what he needed to do to keep the Brewers in front. He worked out of a jam in the first inning where Aranda and Chandler Simpson reached with back-to-back singles. However, Misiorowski got Caminero to line into a double play to end the inning. He allowed a single run in the fourth and exited after the fifth having allowed four hits to go along with three strikeouts.

The Brewers added an insurance run in the seventh on a run-scoring single by Jackson Chourio that pushed the lead to 3-1. Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined for three scoreless innings in relief before turning things over to Megill in the ninth. Ashby has been one of the best pitchers in the postseason running his streak to 14 scoreless innings across seven appearances.

The two teams will meet again on Saturday for Game 2 of the series. Logan Henderson will get the start for Milwaukee while Tampa will go with righty ace Drew Rasmussen.

articles.title: Brewers Hold Off Rays in Game 1 Thriller to Take World Series Lead
articles.summary: Yelich Gives Milwaukee an Early Spark The Brewers wasted little time getting on the scoreboard. Christian Yelich delivered an RBI triple in the bottom of the...
articles.body:
The Brewers wasted little time getting on the scoreboard. Christian Yelich delivered an RBI triple in the bottom of the first inning to give Milwaukee a 1-0 lead. William Contreras followed with an RBI single, extending the advantage to 2-0 and immediately putting pressure on Tampa Bay's pitching staff.

On the mound, rookie right-hander Jacob Misiorowski made an impression early. He fired a 103.5 mph pitch, setting a World Series velocity record in the pitch-tracking era. His electric fastball gave Milwaukee a major weapon as the Brewers attempted to keep Tampa Bay's lineup under control.

The Rays finally broke through in the fourth inning when Liam Hicks grounded out to bring home a run, cutting the deficit to 2-1. Tampa Bay continued looking for opportunities, but Milwaukee's pitching and defense limited the damage.

Milwaukee regained a two run cushion in the seventh inning. Jackson Chourio delivered an RBI single to make it 3-1, giving the Brewers a valuable insurance run heading into the final innings.

The hit proved crucial as Tampa Bay continued battling. The Rays threatened in the ninth, cutting the deficit to one run when Liam Hicks brought home a runner. Tampa Bay also attempted a double steal to put the tying run in scoring position, creating a tense situation for Milwaukee's bullpen.

However, the Brewers managed to escape the late threat and secure the final out, protecting the narrow lead and sending the home crowd into celebration.

The 3-2 victory gives Milwaukee a 1-0 lead in the World Series and provides an important confidence boost after a long postseason journey. The Brewers received contributions from their offense early, added a key insurance run late and held on when the Rays made their final push.

Yelich and Contreras set the tone in the opening inning, while Chourio's seventh-inning hit ultimately helped make the difference.

Milwaukee will now look to carry that momentum into Game 2. With the opening victory secured, the Brewers have an opportunity to put additional pressure on Tampa Bay and move one step closer to the franchise's first World Series championship.

articles.title: 3 adjustments Valkyries must make to bounce back in WNBA Finals Game 4 vs. Dream
articles.summary: ATLANTA – The Golden State Valkyries are itching to get back onto the court and under the spotlight, down 2-1 heading into Game 4 of the WNBA Finals. The ang...
articles.body:
ATLANTA – The Golden State Valkyries are itching to get back onto the court and under the spotlight, down 2-1 heading into Game 4 of the WNBA Finals . The angst, the emotion, the frustration, the fight– the Valkyries are dying to unleash it all and exorcise their demons from their ugly 97-71 Game 3 loss to the Atlanta Dream.

"We're hungry," Valkyries forward Kaila Charles said at the team's Friday afternoon practice. "This has been the longest two days ever. I'm ready to play again. But I think our spirits are really high. We understand what we need to do, and we're excited to get another chance."

Game 4 is a chance Golden State doesn't take lightly, a window of opportunity that can and will close in an instant. Either they tie the series up heading back to their raucous home crowd in Ballhalla, or they find themselves in the quicksand of a 3-1 deficit and on the brink of their magic run to the Finals dissipating into dust.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

As such, the Valkyries require making some major adjustments to stifle the Dream, who've set the tone the entire series thus far. From Angel Reese steamrolling them to the cup and giving them the "petite" gesture, along the way to Atlanta as a whole squeezing the life out of the Golden State offense and forcing them into uncharacteristic turnovers, it's adapt or go extinct for the Valkyries at this juncture of the series.

So here are three aspects of the series the Valkyries need to address and adjust to even things up at 2-2 and get back to their brand of unrelenting, strength-in-numbers basketball.

The Valkyries must uncork the halfcourt offense

It's not surprising that Golden State's been rendered completely ineffective in the halfcourt this series. After all, the Dream boast the Defensive Player of the Year and have the length and athleticism to blunt a lot of what the Valkyries like to do best, specifically their drive-and-kick, stampede actions – where a player catches the ball on the run as they cut after the initiator draws the defense.

Nor has it been a surprise when it seems like every single shot Golden State attempts has a hand in their face or a Dream defender all the way in their airspace– the Valkyries boasted one of the toughest shot difficulties all season long, with their best shotmakers having some of the lower expected field goal percentages in the league.

But it has been a decisive factor in the tenor of this series. Atlanta has completely taken away Golden State's transition opportunities, the part of the game where their offense is cleanest and when the Valkyries can unload the avalanche on teams, making their halfcourt execution even more important. So far this series, they haven't come close to cracking the Dream's shell defense, designed to gap their drives and force them into 1-on-1 iso basketball.

So the Valkyries know what they need to do: score more points in the halfcourt. Obviously. But how they do that is the real conundrum.

Because while Gabby Williams has risen to a star-level talent these playoffs, her on-ball will just never draw two defenders to her in the way a truly A1 offensive talent demands, which is not a knock on her, just a statement of fact for how Atlanta has defended her this series. And while it's easy to say "scrap the scheme" when the scheme isn't working, you can't just do that in the middle of a Finals series; you don't have time.

So at this juncture, Golden State is going to have to lean on their strength-in-numbers philosophy to solve the Dream's defense. That could mean leaning more into the depth that has done well offensively this series. Tiffany Hayes seems like the one Valkyrie who can consistently punch the paint. Janelle Salaun came alive in Game 3; at her best, she can overcome a hand in her face and bury any-and-all catch-and-shoot triples.

From Williams' point of view, it comes down to being more decisive, which melds into coach Natalie Nakase's point about cutting down on turnovers. Overall, the Valkyries have been controlling the tempo, reducing possessions, and getting extra possessions from steals and offensive rebounds. Those are key factors that can certainly help loosen up their offensive slog. But the fact of the matter is they'll just need to make some tough buckets. A simple solution, but hard to make a reality with the way Atlanta's defending.

The Valkyries must slow down Angel Reese

On the flip side, and a far more controllable variable than their high-variance offense, is the Valkyries' defense, which still hasn't solved Reese, despite that side of the court being the defining trait of their run to the Finals.

It's not for a lack of effort. Golden State has used center Kiah Stokes with some success, but it comes at the cost of clogging their offense's spacing. And when Stokes hasn't been on the floor, Reese has literally burned everyone else. Aminata Gueye? Torched – and trash-talked along the way. Kayla Thornton? Not big enough and not quick enough. Salaun? Hasn't been fast enough laterally for the quick Reese. Laeticia Amihere? Outmuscled whenever she doesn't have a help defender behind her to deter Reese.

So what's the adjustment? Well, it's not as simple as showing two at Reese or loading up the help behind her like they did to A'ja Wilson in the Las Vegas Aces series.

For one, the Dream are doing a great job putting her in spots that make it terrible tactically to do either of those things, unless you are comfortable with any one of her four teammates getting a wide-open shot, something Wilson didn't really have the luxury of. And for another, it may just be better to let Reese get hers and keep every other Dream player locked up and out of rhythm. The Valkyries' defense got completely worked when Reese started getting everyone else involved. Whether it was her leading the break or finding the right pass when all eyes were on her, she's deadliest when she's bullying the Valkyries enough to send even more resources at her.

That doesn't mean don't guard her. Nakase should probably be matching Stokes minutes with her at this point – and find a way to make her more useful offensively – and Amihere has a case for getting more run against her. Maybe even throw Kaila Charles at her. She's had the most fight and energy of any Valkyrie these Finals, as she didn't back down when she and Rhyne Howard got into it. It also helps that she played with Reese in AAU on Team Takeover in Maryland; she might intuitively remember some age-old secrets to defending her.

But ultimately, Golden State needs to limit her on the offensive boards; she has 11 in the Finals and had five in Game 3. Again, easier said than done against the best rebounder in the league. But those kinds of plays become back-breaking over the course of a game, and if they want to win the possession battle, it behooves the Valkyries to consider boxing her out with even more attention.

The Valkyries must find the fire and get back to Golden State basketball

But X's and O's and tactics aside, the Valkyries believe their shortcomings in Games 2 and 3 all stem from not playing like themselves. And wrapped into that is the way Reese and the Dream have won the mind game battle in how she's fired herself up with the trash talk. Those kinds of things give Atlanta their edge – their motivation. The Valkyries have motivation; it just hasn't translated into their hoops. And they know it .

"We need to have some fire, too," Charles said when asked about how Reese has gone at Gueye specifically and how the Valkyries as a whole deal with those kinds of interactions. "People (don't) necessarily (have to be) trash talkers, but being more physical, imposing our will, and dictating the game that way."

Charles' answer underscores Golden State's most needed adjustment– get back to playing Valkyries basketball and get back to setting the tone. The Dream have taken them away from their identity better than any team has this season. But what makes a team great– what makes a team worthy of a championship– is being unshakable. And being unshakable means finding a way, no matter the circumstances, something the Valkyries have done all season long.

"There's been moments in games this season where it feels like there's no way we're gonna win this," Veronica Burton said. "And you could say that there's no way the Valkyries are gonna be here, whatever it may be. And you find a way, and you will it out, and you do it together, and you grind it out. That's what has allowed us to get here. That's what allowed us to beat LA, or what allowed us to beat Dallas in Game 3 when we're down (16). Like, logistically, it doesn't make much sense, but you come together, and you find a way to do it, and that's what it comes down to."

The heart of a champion rests inside the Valkyries. We've all heard it beat loudly whenever they've defied the odds and upended our expectations. So maybe the biggest adjustment they can make in Game 4 is to revive that pulse. Because if we've learned anything this season, if Burton and her squad have a pulse, they have a fighting chance.

articles.title: Que no te engañen. La silla gaming Soma Chroma es más que luces: es comodidad de alto nivel
articles.summary: Sobre el papel, la Razer Soma Chroma es una de esas sillas gaming que corren el riesgo de parecer más un capricho que otra cosa, puesto que la primera impresión que ofrece es la de una silla muy llamativa que destaca por su iluminación RGB.
articles.body: Sobre el papel, la Razer Soma Chroma es una de esas sillas gaming que corren el riesgo de parecer más un capricho que otra cosa, puesto que la primera impresión que ofrece es la de una silla muy llamativa que destaca por su iluminación RGB. No obstante, esta primera impresión no debe engañarte, puesto que detrás de todo ese muy bonito sistema de iluminación se esconde una silla bastante top que destaca, entre otras cosas, por su ergonomía. Para entenderlo tuve que probarla durante un tiempo, y fue esto lo que me convenció de que su propuesta iba más allá de una silla con luces de una marca a la que ya conocemos. Porque sí, la iluminación RGB es uno de sus factores más destacados. Es lo que, entre otras cosas, le da personalidad, pero lo que realmente importa es que es una silla cómoda, elegante, resistente y muy práctica. Me sorprendió, la verdad. Razer se podría haber conformado con ofrecer un diseño llamativo que justificase su precio, pero decidió ir más allá. Siendo sincero, me alegro de que haya sido de esta manera, porque para mí lo más importante en una silla es que sea cómoda. La ergonomía y la salud de la espalda son los elementos que más importancia deben tener en cualquier producto de estas características y en este caso estamos ante una que cumple con buena nota en ambos. Bien pertrechada con acabados de calidad y un sistema de montaje mucho más sencillo de lo que parece, el resultado final es el de un producto que mezcla ese capricho de iluminación con esa necesidad de estar sentado en una buena silla. Así pues, lo primero que os puedo decir es que estar sentado en ella se siente muy bien. La Soma Chroma viene equipada con espuma de doble densidad curada en frío. En otras palabras, es un sistema que tiene por objetivo ofrecer una sensación mullida mientras se reparte la presión al estar sentado. Si lo traduzco a la práctica, el sentimiento es agradable. Es cómoda. Además, los reposabrazos también están acolchados, por lo que la idea de pasar varias horas sentado frente al ordenador en ella no es un problema. Es más, lo hice y no me sentí pesado en ningún momento. Tanto es así que, a título personal, me parece una de las sillas más cómodas de Razer. No porque el asiento sea blando, ya que no lo es en exceso, sino porque la sensación general es buena. La postura básica es sólida y no resulta incómoda. En ese sentido, ayuda mucho que su respaldo se pueda reclinar hasta 155 grados, lo cual no está nada mal. Cierto es que no es la silla más destacada en ese sentido, y que tampoco está pensada para ello, pero ahí está. Si tuviese que ponerle alguna pega, es que quizá le habría sentado bien la capacidad de ajustar más tanto este aspecto como el resto de condicionantes a la hora de estar sentado. Por ejemplo, el soporte lumbar no se puede ajustar en posición o intensidad, y aunque tiene una curvatura integrada muy agradable, la posibilidad de ajustarlo siempre es un extra. Sucede lo mismo con los reposabrazos, que solo disponen de regulación de altura y lateral. Pese a ello, no considero que sea una mala silla. Más bien todo lo contrario. Es realmente cómoda, por lo que estos detalles son más bien aspectos que podrían mejorar, pero que no devalúan el resultado final. Es muy buena silla. Luego está el tema de la iluminación. Si quieres darle un toque extra a tu setup y que sea más resultón, lo cierto es que la Soma Chroma puede ser justo lo que estés buscando. El acabado con silueta deportiva en negro y detalles verdes con iluminación RGB la convierten en una de las sillas más espectaculares del mercado en términos visuales. Es perfecta para streaming y grabación. Pero su acabado gaming no la hace menos elegante. No es un conjunto de colores resultones sin más, sino que mantiene la sobriedad propia que le pedimos a una marca como Razer. Tomando en consideración todos estos aspectos, y con un precio recomendado de 529,99 euros, la Soma Chroma es una gran silla. Hay que entender que se trata de un producto premium, por lo que lo más importante es considerar si es lo que buscas o no. Razer tiene un abanico muy amplio de opciones y esta, posiblemente, esté más pensada para los que buscan darle a su setup un toque extra para que sus grabaciones, streamings, etc., sean incluso más llamativos. Pese a ello, no debemos pensar que se orienta solo a este aspecto, porque el acabado es muy bueno y la ergonomía es de alto nivel. Cumple en ambos ámbitos con buena nota. En definitiva, la Razer Soma Chroma es mucho más que colores. Es una silla elegante, resistente, práctica y, sobre todo, muy cómoda. Las luces son la carta de presentación, pero es el conjunto lo que hace que termine convenciendo.

articles.title: 12 Anime Worth Watching This Fall
articles.summary: From a return to Night City to a legendary blacksmith and bizarre race, we run down the new and returning anime titles you need to check out.
articles.body:
A return to Night City, a legendary blacksmith, and a bizarre race are what you can expect this fall anime season. There's a new season full of anime to check out this Fall like the return of the award-winning Cyberpunk Edgerunners , the hilarious Overgeared, and the highly anticipated continuation of Steel Ball Run JoJo's Bizarre Adventure . Across Crunchyroll, HIDIVE, Hulu, and Netflix, as well as others, there are a lot of places to enjoy anime at the moment.

Check out some anticipated series in the video above or the slideshow gallery below, followed by the full list of new Fall season 2026 anime and where to watch them in the U.S. and their respective streaming platforms. Anime listed are available now unless otherwise stated.

Best New Anime to Watch (Fall Season 2026)

The highly anticipated sports series Aoashi returns with Season 2! It’s been a few years now since we last saw Ashito and teammates attempt to rise through the ranks of the Tokyo City football club. Now that Ashito has made a good showing, the competition ramps up yet again. TMS Entertainment, known for Dr. Stone and Yowamushi Pedal, takes up the animation production reins this season. Unlike Blue Lock, but similar to Haikyu, Aoashi is much more grounded. So if you’re a fan of sports anime along those lines, now’s the time to get on the pitch and check this out. Aoashi Season 2 is available now on Crunchyroll.

Speaking of sports anime, Blue Box is back with its Season 2! This sports anime also has romance, so there’s been quite a bit of drama since we last saw Taiki and the gang navigate their feelings. Electric Circus, a newer studio composed of some former Telecom Animation Film staff, is taking on animation production this season. We can’t wait to see how these relationships progress this fall after leaving us with major decisions last season. If you’re looking to take a break from the many action-packed series out now, this series is worth checking out. Blue Box Season 2 is available now on Netflix.

A new romance series dropping this fall is Firefly Wedding. The series follows Satoko, the daughter of a prestigious family who is navigating marriage proposals while dealing with a secret health issue. After an unfortunate event, she negotiates for her life by proposing marriage to a killer. David Production, known for JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure and Fire Force, is at the helm of this series, so expect some crazy action as these spouses-to-be prepare for an unlikely wedding. Firefly Wedding is available now on Crunchyroll.

Looking for a fun fantasy series this fall? Overgeared is the anime for you this season! The series follows Shin, a player in a popular fantasy VR game which offers opportunities to make money in the real world. He’s been struggling for a while now, but falls upon a once-in-a-lifetime chance to become a legendary blacksmith class. With these newfound abilities, he can turn around his luck even though he isn’t super exceptional in other categories. J.C. Staff, the studio behind The Disastrous Life of Saiki K. and Bakuman, is handling animation production on this series. So far, it’s been a hilarious ride as Shin learns more about his class and how he can use it in this dangerous fantasy game world. The series follows Rein, an enchanter who gets laid off from his guild after serving his purpose. Soon after, he takes back all his enchantments and imbues his own plain gear with the same magic, making him a force to be reckoned with. P.A. Works, known for Shirobako and Skip to Loafer, is heading animation on this new series. Seeing Rein dive head first into an adventure without any clue of what he’s doing has been the highlight this early in the season. It’s an especially good time when his newfound ally, Lily, freaks out about all the careless chaos he brings. The Laid-Off Cheat-Granting Mage Enjoys a Second Lease on Life is available now on Crunchyroll.

The supernatural 2007 manga Psyren is getting an anime adaptation this fall season. The series follows Ageha, a young student who tries to help a friend and unknowingly gets involved with a mysterious world filled with monsters. Satelight, the studio behind Log Horizon and Macross F, is taking on production for this long-awaited series. If you’re interested in seeing what the fuss is about after all these years, you can check out Psyren, available now on Crunchyroll.

One of the most striking anime this fall season is Fool Night. The series follows Toshiro, a struggling man contemplating difficult choices in a dystopian world trapped in constant darkness. Since there’s no sunlight, society has developed a way to sustain life and oxygen by turning humans into plants. The studios behind Mobile Suit Gundam and March Comes in Like a Lion, Sunrise and Shaft, are joining forces for what looks to be a visually impressive anime. Based on the teasers so far, there is a beautiful emphasis on lights in this dark world. Alongside the body horror of the plant technology, there are some intriguing bits here to get sci-fans excited for the upcoming premiere. Fool Night will be available on Netflix November 26.

Speaking of dystopian worlds, Cyberpunk Edgerunners returns with a Season 2 this fall! The series has a whole new cast of characters this time around, so we may or may not see someone like Lucy this season. Studio Trigger returns yet again to this award-winning series, and it shows in what we’ve seen so far. Between the amazing character designs and the gritty Night City action, Season 2 is looking to impress yet again. Cyberpunk Edgerunners Season 2 is available now on Netflix.

The highly anticipated return of Black Clover is finally here with Season 2! It’s been about five years since we last saw Asta and friends, and here they prepare to rescue their beloved captain from the latest big baddie. Studio Pierrot is back again to lead animation production, so expect more of the sleek, action-packed battles we’ve seen before. If you’re interested in the series, there’s a bit of catching up to do, but now’s the time to really get into this popular shonen series. Black Clover Season 2 is available now on Crunchyroll.

articles.title: Avengers: Doomsday Teaser Reveals Who Was Edited Out of the First Trailer, Fans Say
articles.summary: Marvel fans say the new Avengers: Doomsday teaser might have revealed who was edited out of its first trailer.
articles.body:
Marvel fans say the new Avengers: Doomsday teaser might have revealed who was edited out of its first trailer.

Marvel Studios didn't not reveal more from its December team-up movie when the Doomsday baseball teaser premiered during Game 1 of the 2026 World Series last night. Focusing more on letting Pedro Pascal's Reed Richards throw Joseph Quinn's Johnny Storm a stretchy pitch as MLB players did their best to fit in, the minute-long TV spot felt more like a cute crossover than an opportunity for new footage – but that doesn't mean fans aren't still all over it.

In between the shots of the Fantastic Four's Earth-828 are, occasionally, what amounts to a few precious seconds of new footage from Avengers: Doomsday. With less than two months left to go until the premiere, Marvel really only took the time to highlight some funny interactions between Steve Rogers (Chris Evans) and characters like Ant-Man (Paul Rudd) and Thor (Chris Hemsworth).

Worlds collide ⚾ An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀 Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18 — MLB (@MLB) October 24, 2026

Worlds collide ⚾ An exclusive preview of Marvel's new Avengers movie assembles Bryce Harper, Freddie Freeman, Jacob Misiorowski, Junior Caminero and Randy Arozarena 👀 Avengers: Doomsday arrives in theaters everywhere December 18

It's…not much. While you might think Steve taking a jab at Thor while wielding Mjolnir is the standout moment, some eagle-eyed fans think it's the scene the former Captain America shares with Ant-Man that we should be paying attention to.

Let's take a step back. You might remember Marvel fans doing what they do best by looking for clues tucked into the original Doomsday trailer . One shot that caught a lot of attention was an image showing the New Avengers having a meeting with old heroes and the Fantastic Four . A gap between the Earth-828 heroes led many to believe Marvel had, as it's been known to do before, edited out an important character from the scene.

The World Series teaser took viewers back and showed that scene from a new perspective, bringing Steve Rogers along as a plus one. The quick shot of Evans' character showed that he's almost certainly standing next to Ebon Moss-Bachrach's Ben Grimm as he does his best to entertain Scott Lang. With Evans unseen in the previously questionable look at the scene, Marvel fans believe Steve Rogers was the character Marvel was trying to hide all along.

Steve being next to Ben confirms he was edited out of the first trailer. He is next to Ben, Sam and Scott — Shaane (@bussdownhendrix) October 24, 2026

Steve being next to Ben confirms he was edited out of the first trailer. He is next to Ben, Sam and Scott

"Yup, and Doom is edited out too," another fan said , referencing a theory that Doctor Doom may appear as an ally during the events of the film. "I wonder if they will show it in the trailers, hopefully they do just a tiny bit."

And ta-da: We finally seem to have our answer – but why? Why would Marvel edit out a character that fans are already well aware had a role to play in Doomsday? It's confusing, especially considering Steve does eventually show up later in the trailer he's believed to have been edited out of.

On the other side of things are those still trying to determine if the person we've seen wielding Mjolnir is even Steve Rogers at all. One popular fan theory that has gained more traction as Evans' role is once again put under the microscope is that his character is actually Tom Hiddleston's Loki in disguise. Some also suspect that the original trailer wasn't ever edited in the first place, with this new footage simply showing the same scene but a few seconds before or after that shot of questionable positioning.

Was Marvel playing with its hero positioning just to give its first trailer a bit more punch toward the end, is there more mystery to solve, or are fans maybe looking too much into things? That's the main conversation fans are having in the aftermath of just a few frames of new Doomsday footage.

Holdup — Best of Marvel (@BestMarvelU) October 24, 2026

this sounds exactly like something Loki would say to Thor as steve rogers 😭 — hailey* ౨ৎ (@sentrynation) October 24, 2026

this sounds exactly like something Loki would say to Thor as steve rogers 😭

"In the new trailer, I can't be the only one, Steve's face or something looks weird like it kept changing in each scene or something else," one theorist said . "I can't quite put my finger on it but something about him is off."

As ridiculous as some of this might sound, Marvel has absolutely played with pre-release footage to throw fans off the scent of big reveals before. Marketing materials released in the lead-up to Avengers: Infinity War in 2018 provide a few of the most notable examples, with many seemingly important scenes featured in trailers completely cut from the final version of the film. Searching for potential edits with a fine-tooth comb is also something Marvel fans did ahead of the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day .

Unfortunately, we'll have to wait until Avengers: Doomsday comes to theaters december 18, 2026, to find out which theories are correct and which ones didn't quite pan out. In the meantime, you can read about the latest addition to the film's already-stacked cast. You can also see how David Harbour did his best to walk back potentially spoiler-y comments he made earlier this year.

articles.title: Elden Ring Movie's Budget Reportedly $200 Million, Almost 3x More Expensive Than A24's Marty Supreme
articles.summary: Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie reportedly carries a hefty budget of almost $200 million, making it A24's most expensive movie ever – and it's not close.
articles.body:
Alex Garland's Elden Ring movie reportedly carries a hefty budget of almost $200 million, making it A24's most expensive movie ever – and it's not close.

Background information on the live-action adaptation of FromSoftware and George R.R. Martin's 2022 RPG was shared in a Wall Street Journal report. The site stated that, according to its sources, Elden Ring's budget is "nearly $200 million."

That makes it far and away the most expensive movie for the arthouse film-focused company, which has built a reputation for delivering memorable projects on more modest budgets for the last 14 years. Should Elden Ring's reported budget prove accurate, it would mean Garland's film falls in line with Marvel movies like Spider-Man: No Way Home ($200 million via Variety ) and Jurassic World Rebirth ($180 million via The Hollywood Reporter ).

As seen in 2025's Marty Supreme , that's a far cry from A24's usual strategy. The Timothée Chalamet-led, Josh Safdie-directed drama made headlines ahead of its release for being the most expensive film the company had produced at $70 million (via Deadline ).

That puts Elden Ring at nearly three times the cost of A24's next-most-expensive picture. Garland's Civil War supposedly cost $50 million before that, according to Variety . Dwayne 'The Rock' Johnson's The Smashing Machine reportedly carried a similar budget. In other words, nothing really comes close to A24's first major swing into the world of video game movie adaptations.

For now, we know little about Elden Ring ahead of its 2028 premiere, so it's hard to say exactly why it costs so much. Earlier this year, the movie studio announced the film had a pretty stacked cast, which includes familiar faces like Kit Connor (X-Men, Warfare), Cailee Spaeny (Alien: Romulus, Civil War), Nick Offerman (The Last of Us, Parks and Recreation), Havana Rose Liu (Tuner, Bottoms), and more. Early production photos then teased faithful recreations of some iconic sets, with more making their way to the internet not long after .

The Elden Ring movie's big budget may not have always been the plan for what's shaping up to, one way or another, be a massive release for A24. Previous reports had the live-action fantasy flick pinned at just more than $100 million , suggesting either that initial rumors were inaccurate or Garland's budget somehow ballooned over the course of production. Filming finally wrapped in July of this year.

The Elden Ring movie was announced in May 2025 and is expected to premiere March 3, 2028. It will probably be a little while longer before we see any official images or a trailer, so in the meantime, you can read about how actor and Dark Souls superfan Peter Serafinowicz landed a role in the film .
