articles.title: 104-year-old Brewers fan makes second accurate score prediction
articles.summary: Ruth Werning, 104, has now accurately predicted the winning Brewers' score not once, but twice, in the post-season.
articles.body:
Charlotte Werning Kolby thinks she should be placing bets.

Her 104-year-old mother Ruth Werning has now accurately predicted the Milwaukee Brewers' winning score not once, but twice, on their post-season journey.

First, Werning told a WISN-TV reporter the Brewers would win 6-2 in Game 3 of the National League Championship Series against the Los Angeles Dodgers Oct. 14.

Days later, Werning told the Milwaukee Journal Sentinel her World Series Game 1 prediction: Brewers would beat the Tampa Bay Devil Rays, 3-2.

For a few seconds of Friday night's chaotic ninth inning , some of the Brewers players, an umpire, a broadcaster, thousands of fans and, apparently, whoever controls American Family Field's post-game fireworks, would have said Werning's Game 1 prediction was off.

They all thought shortstop Cooper Pratt caught the ball with his foot still on second base before turning a double-play to secure a 3-1 win and take a 1-0 series lead.

But Werning was right after all, even if it caused the 43,250 fans in attendance and Brewers Nation a few more tense minutes. But after a challenge on the play from Rays manager Kevin Cash, a replay showed Pratt's foot came off second base.

Then Brewers pitcher Trevor Megill struck out Jonny DeLuca to actually close out the game, and the Brewers won 3-2, just as Werning predicted.

"I wish I were a betting person," daughter Werning Kolby said the morning after World Series Game 1.

Her mom didn't get her Game 4 NLCS prediction right, but still, these two correct predictions are "more than kind of crazy," Werning Kolby said.

Ruth Werning didn't stay up to watch the end of Game 1. Werning woke up "on cloud nine" about her Milwaukee Brewers winning, according to her daughter, who checked in with her mom on the phone during breakfast. The pair are still game to attend a Brewers World Series game in person, if the opportunity presents itself.

Werning doesn't make predictions like this often, her daughter said. But she does have a strong intuition.

"She's got a hotline to God, I'll tell you that," Werning Kolby the morning of Oct. 24.

So, what does Werning guess will happen in Game 2 of the World Series?

Werning Kolby relayed her mom's prediction over the phone.

"They will win, and the score will be 3-1 Brewers," Werning Kolby said.

She said her mom sounded quite confident.

articles.title: Big Boi continues Atlanta's excellent run with halftime show for WNBA Finals Game 4
articles.summary: Big Boi joins the superstar list of performers for the WNBA Finals in Atlanta. The OutKast rapper was the star of the halftime show for Game 4.
articles.body:
A big stage calls for a big halftime show performance.

And that's exactly what happened for Game 4 of the WNBA Finals between the Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream when Atlanta icon Big Boi took the court with the Valkyries up 42-26. He rocked a massive brown fur coat and was accompanied by fellow ATL legend Sleepy Brown, who donned a gray fur coat. The two performed their OutKast collaboration "The Way You Move" sans André 3000 and the duo's other hits "So Fresh, So Clean" and "Ms. Jackson."

Continuing the streak of Atlanta greatness, Pastor Troy performed earlier during a break in play. He had the crowd jumping up and down to his classic song, "No Mo Play in G.A.," which was an inspiration for Archie Eversole's sports anthem "We Ready."

Ahead of tipoff, actress Crystal Renee Hayslett performed the national anthem for Game 4.

The WNBA has been impressing with their selection of superstars for the game-day festivities this Finals. Alanis Morissette performed the national anthem for Game 2. Q Parker of 112 did the pre-game performance for Game 3 , the first matchup of the series in Atlanta. The Dream's first home game featured other hip-hop heavyweights, including performances from Skooly and 2 Chainz and a halftime show headlined by Quavo.

Earlier in the series, there was controversy surrounding the national anthem because fans were confused when players ran off the court before and after the song. Per WNBA policy, players have the choice to attend the ceremony or not.

articles.title: Call of Duty Movie Director Teases Story That Explores 'the Cost of War,' Praises Modern Warfare Characters
articles.summary: Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."
articles.body:
Call of Duty movie director Peter Berg has teased more details from his live-action film, promising an adaptation with "a very strong soul" that explores "the cost of war."

The filmmaker behind Skydance-Paramount's upcoming reimagining of Activision's massive first-person shooter series dived into his thoughts on the franchise during an interview with ComicBook . We already know the Call of Duty movie will focus on the Modern Warfare portion of the FPS universe , and it sounds like Berg and writer Taylor Sheridan have already looked to the games it's based on for inspiration.

"So Modern Warfare, if you really look at the missions, and the storylines, and the characters – like Captain Price, and Soap, and Ghost, and Alex – these are complicated humans," Berg said. "These are not – and no disrespect – cartoon characters or comic books. These are very nuanced storylines; like, there's a real soul to the Modern Warfare universe…

"And, yes, there's violence, and there's hardware, and equipment, and there's killing – but underneath it I think the game, and the craters of the game, are really looking at the cost of war, the cost of having to be a warrior who's, for whatever reason, chosen to put himself between real danger and the rest of us, and the burden that these guys carry."

Berg seems to be putting in the work to nail a Modern Warfare story for the big screen, but not every fan is convinced that he's the right guy for the job . That's mostly because he had some not-so-nice things to say about gaming back in 2013. When asked for his take on video games based on war at the time, he said, called them "pathetic," using the term, "keyboard courage."

"I think anyone that sits around playing video games for four hours... It's weak," Berg elaborated at the time. "Get out, do something."

These days he's changed his tune, and judging by his affection for characters like Captain Price and Ghost, he's hoping to do right by Modern Warfare and its fans. His upcoming film, The Mosquito Bowl, is a sports-war film set to premiere later this month. His vision for the Call of Duty movie will start to take shape after that.

Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 Campaign Screenshots

"And that’s real stuff," Berg added when talking about Modern Warfare's connection to the real-life cost of war. "This is not just 'Hey, let’s shoot them all up and shoot popcorn!' Like, there’s a soul underneath it, that I understand that Taylor Sheridan understands, and I think probably not quite as graphically violent as Mosquito Bowl, but there will be a very strong soul, and consequence of war within the film, called 'duty.'"

The Modern Warfare universe most recently expanded with the release of Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 4 , which concluded Activision and Infinity Ward's reboot story when it launched yesterday. Its story has been called one of the darker entries the franchise has offered in recent memory.

The Call of Duty movie, meanwhile, is set to come to theaters June 30, 2028. Additional plot details have not been revealed, though fans have already been busy sharing their hopes for who may play familiar (and unconfirmed) characters like Captain Price, Ghost, and more. It's a year that seems set to be big for video game adaptations, with an Elden Ring film also set to release a few months prior. A Battlefield movie is also in the works .

articles.title: Valkyries switch things up, grind out Game 4 win to even WNBA Finals with Dream
articles.summary: ATLANTA — After getting outplayed in the previous two games of the WNBA Finals and a majority of Game 1, the Golden State Valkyries had to reevaluate their c...
articles.body:
ATLANTA — After getting outplayed in the previous two games of the WNBA Finals and a majority of Game 1, the Golden State Valkyries had to reevaluate their commitment to the identity that led them to the league's biggest stage.

A playoff series is all about adjustments, and it was time for the Valkyries to shake things up.

Down 2-1, Golden State busted out a full bag of new tricks, introducing just enough chaos to win 67-62 and tie the series at 2-all heading back to San Francisco. The Valkyries shifted their starting lineup for the first time this postseason, trimmed their rotation and played a heavier diet of zone in Game 4.

It resulted in Golden State winning the possession battle and keeping Atlanta out of transition. Sprinkle in some jumpers for the Valkyries' starting backcourt — Gabby Williams had a team-high 17 points, and Veronica Burton had a critical 3-pointer late in the fourth quarter — and the road team had just enough to eke out a win.

Golden State built a 16-point lead by halftime, but the Dream whittled the deficit down to two possessions at multiple points in the second half. One decisive sequence came with about four minutes remaining. Atlanta played excellent defense, but Burton hit a deep 3-pointer as the shot clock expired to push the lead back to nine, and Angel Reese missed two open shots at the rim on the ensuing possession.

When the Dream cut the lead to five with 1:36 to play on a Reese lay-up, it was once again Burton who hit a fadeaway to extend the advantage back to seven and secure the win for the Valkyries.

"(Burton's) our heart and soul of the team," Golden State coach Natalie Nakase said. "She said, I got it, I got the isolation. She just attacked her matchup and closed it."

The Valkyries subbed out two of their underperforming starters (Kayla Thornton and Cecilia Zandalasini) and reaped the rewards. Kaila Charles' energy helped Golden State set a strong tone early — Nakase likes to say that Charles is always on full throttle — and Tiffany Hayes getting downhill helped break Atlanta's defensive shell.

Charles was a team-high plus-14 in her 28 minutes and won her matchup with Naz Hillmon, keeping the Dream power forward from establishing herself offensively. Hayes scored 13 points, with seven coming in the fourth quarter as the Valkyries staved off another strong second-half effort from Atlanta. The Dream could keep everyone in front except Hayes, who repeatedly got to the basket and finished well.

"(Hayes) is a dawg, she's so fast," Williams said. "Her being able to come alive in that fourth quarter really sealed the game for us."

Zandalasini and Thornton still contributed off the bench. The Italian guard had her best game of the series with 10 points and three steals, finally making an impact defensively. After she entered the game in the first quarter, Golden State ripped off a 10-0 run, taking the lead for the remainder of the game.

Thornton had only 3 points but was part of a team effort to limit Reese, using her strength to affect the Atlanta superstar more than she had been able to in previous games.

"Just wanted to change it up," Nakase said. "The nice thing about our team is, I don't care who starts. No one cares. … We do that because we have a really selfless team, an egoless team."

Golden State has emphasized strength in numbers throughout the season, going deeper into its rotation than any other playoff team. The Valkyries have used 11 players in the first quarter of this series, a stark contrast to Atlanta, which has mostly relied on seven.

Game 4 marked a significant change in Golden State's approach. Laeticia Amihere and Aminata Gueye were excised from the rotation, and Janelle Salaün and Kaitlyn Chen combined for fewer than five minutes. The Valkyries essentially matched seven with seven. In doing so, they gave Atlanta no weak links to attack.

"Just did what it took to win," Nakase said about the short rotation.

Reese had dominated Golden State's backup centers, so Nakase didn't play them. Instead, she relied on more zone defense when Kiah Stokes was off the court in an attempt to deny the ball to Reese. The Dream were involving Chen in every offensive action when she was on the court, so she was limited to a two-minute stint to start the fourth quarter when Burton desperately needed a rest before the closing stretch.

Atlanta's offense had less flow to start the game without any obvious holes in the defense. It also helped that Zandalasini provided more defensive playmaking than she had in the first three games, taking the implicit message that her move to the bench was because of her earlier shortcomings on that end.

Atlanta fuels its offense with its defense, forcing turnovers to get out in transition. When that well dried up Saturday — Golden State committed nine turnovers leading to eight points — the Dream needed more scoring from its stars in the half court. That didn't happen.

Allisha Gray got in early foul trouble, picking up two fouls in the first four minutes and then picking up her third on the very next possession just as Atlanta was considering subbing her out. Coach Karl Smesko is more lenient with foul trouble than other WNBA coaches, often allowing his players to remain on the court to stay in rhythm. "They're keeping score for 40 minutes, so if you sit them out for 10 minutes, you may have protected them from fouling out, but you still were without them for 10 minutes," Smesko said earlier in the series.

Unfortunately for Gray, she never found her flow in the 22 minutes she played. She shot 1 of 7 from the field and missed all four of her 3-pointers, including an open look with 64 seconds to play that would have pulled the Dream within two.

Reese also had her worst game of the series, tallying 8 points on 2-of-12 shooting and nine rebounds. Stokes, who already has a WNBA Finals record with 14 blocks this series, has made things difficult for Reese, but the Atlanta center was also ineffective against Stokes' backups. In addition to her poor finishing, Reese also committed two offensive fouls. She only attempted one 3-pointer despite having more opportunities, allowing the Golden State defense to sit back.

As she did after Game 1, Reese was loath to give any credit to the Valkyries, instead taking the blame for her performance.

"I think it was me," Reese said. "I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn't take my time and finish around the basket like I've been doing the last two games. It happens, and I'm just looking forward to the next game."

Atlanta's most consistent source of offense has been getting to the foul line, but the Dream shot just 22 of 31 on free throws. As Reese noted postgame, if they made their foul shots, they would be headed back to Golden State up 3-1.

The tempo of Game 4 once again matched how the Valkyries want to play. They limited Atlanta's second-chance points and total field-goal attempts, with the Dream's shot total (54) their lowest of the series. Golden State was disciplined in holding on to the ball and preventing Atlanta from running in the open court.

The Valkyries also didn't try to run in transition themselves. Even though they turned over the Dream 18 times, they only attempted six shots on fast breaks, choosing instead to string out the shot clock. Nakase said pregame that they had been trying to punch too frequently in their two losses and needed to take a break. On Saturday, that led to them resetting their possessions rather than trying to keep pace with Atlanta.

It was fitting that Golden State's biggest shots of the game came late in the clock. The Valkyries' advantage comes from their patience. After the longest gap between games in this series, that patience has them even and once again with home-court advantage.

articles.title: Angel Reese explains Game 4 Dream struggles: 'It happens'
articles.summary: Angel Reese wasn't at her best on Saturday in Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.
articles.body:
Atlanta Dream superstar forward Angel Reese didn't have her best game at home on Saturday during Game 4 of the WNBA Finals.

The Valkyries evened the playoff series 2-2 with a 67-62 win, sending the series back to Golden State for Game 5. Reese only scored eight points and recorded nine rebounds in the game, which showed a step down from her sensational performances throughout the first three games of this year's WNBA Finals.

After the game, Reese explained why she didn't feel she wasn't quite as effective as she has been in this championship series.

"I think I rushed a lot of my shots, and I didn't take my time and finish around the basket like I've been doing in the last three games," Reese said in the postgame presser. "It happens, and I'm just looking forward to the next game, and I'll just be better."

Reese has proved why she's one of the best players in the WNBA in this playoff run. For Atlanta to get where it wants to go, the team will need a strong rebound from Reese once Game 5 tips off on Monday.

Game 5 will be at 8 p.m. ET in San Francisco on USA Network for broadcast and Peacock for streaming.

articles.title: James Gunn Defends the DCU's Approach to Interconnected Stories, Doesn't Want Movies Like Clayface to Exist Just to 'Set Up' Crossovers
articles.summary: DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.
articles.body:
DC Studios co-chairman James Gunn has defended the DCU's approach to interconnected stories, saying he doesn't want movies like Clayface to exist just to "set up" crossovers.

Clayface poured into the DCU when it brought the tragic story of Matt Hagen (Tom Rhys Harries) to theaters yesterday. A bloody body horror movie with a firm R rating, its October release date makes sense as it molded its way into the comic book movie universe with a more adult story, but not everyone is happy with the film's place in the universe.

Despite solid scores from critics and fans (IGN gave it a 7/10 review ), there are DC watchers who have continued to complain that executives like Gunn and co-chairman Peter Safran haven't done a good job of using smaller stories to build toward bigger tie-in projects. For reference, the DCU technically started with animated series Creature Commandos before heading to theaters with Superman . Peacemaker Season 2, Supergirl , Lanterns , and Clayface then followed.

While standalone Wonder Woman and Batman movies are in the cards, projects like The People v. Gorilla Grodd seem to be further along than most, with crossover moments mostly limited so far. So, what gives? Gunn has an easy answer that might leave impatient fans wanting more, but for him, it's a solution that will keep the DCU telling quality stories for years to come.

"I couldn't agree more," he said when replying to a fan defending the cinematic universe on Threads. "DCU is just an alternate universe; we can enter at any location or time and tell THAT story. I dislike the idea that individual stories aren't meaningful unless they lead to something else."

Gunn continued, saying it's "strange" to see "people not understanding this" considering Star Wars has taken a similar approach for decades. He did admit Disney's sci-fi franchise may not have the "tonal variety" of something like the DCU , which has so far ping-ponged between serious drama and action to comedy and, most recently, horror. Still, he wants fans to know that, no matter how different each movie or show may be, there is still connective tissue holding them together.

"The Superman Saga starts with Superman and travels into Man of Tomorrow and onward, and contains many characters we've introduced in other stories," he continued in a follow-up post . "But that doesn't mean those other stories only exist to set up what's happening there. I would love people to be seeing Clayface because it's a great, fun horror movie unto itself, not because of where else Clayface will show up three movies from now."

While not everyone is pleased that DC Studios doesn't want to dive head first into crossover event films, one of the reasons others have actually been excited for Clayface is its promise to weave its way into the universe with a new Gotham City. We won't talk about whether Batman or Bruce Wayne make any appearances here , but with plenty of footage taking viewers through one of DC's most iconic locations, it's clear Gunn and co. are more interested in continuing to lay a worthy foundation rather than speeding into a big team-up movie like the Justice League .

Gunn took his time on social media today to touch base on a few other projects in the works. Creature Commandos Season 2, for example , will arrive after Man of Tomorrow's premiere next year. Speaking of the Superman sequel, a small group of people has now seen director's cuts of the film , with Gunn calling the process "exciting" as he tries "to recut over the week and screen the latest version for a few new eyes every Friday."

9 DC Graphic Novels You Should Read to Understand James Gunn's DCU

Meanwhile, Elseworlds sequel, The Batman Part 2 , is still seemingly on track for its February 18, 2028, release date despite recent behind-the-scenes shuffling . For an update on the status of the DCU's Batman, you can click here . Finally, for everything else in the DC movie pipeline, we've got you covered here .

articles.title: Frelick homer sparks Brewers rally for 2-0 World Series lead over Rays
articles.summary: Poised hitting and an unflappable bullpen guided a Milwaukee Brewers rally past the Tampa Bay Rays on Saturday in Game 2 of the 2026 World Series.
articles.body:
Oct. 24 (UPI) -- Sal Frelick whipped his wrists through the zone and splintered a fastball over the center field fence for a near-earthquake-triggering. game-tying home run, guiding a thrilling Milwaukee Brewers rally past the Tampa Bay Rays in Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday in Milwaukee.

The Brewers, who trailed 4-0 in the first inning, leaned on a dominant bullpen as their bats warmed throughout the 5-4 victory at American Field Field. With their seventh comeback win this postseason, they moved within two victories of their first World Series crown.

"Regardless of if we are down or up, that chip-away mentality is just how our offense is designed," Frelick said on the Fox broadcast.

Each team packed the base paths with early traffic, but the Rays capitalized most off that live lumber.

Left fielder Chandler Simpson drove in designated hitter Yandy Diaz for Game 2's first run in the first inning. Third baseman Junior Caminero plated Simpson with a single in the next at-bat. Catcher Liam Hicks followed with a 411-foot, two-run homer to give the Rays a lead they kept until the sixth inning.

But the early electricity shorted, as Brewers pitchers did not allow another run.

The Brewers cut the deficit in half through RBI singles from catcher William Contreras and center fielder Garrett Mitchell off Rays ace Drew Rasmussen in the bottom of the first frame. Brewers shortstop Cooper Pratt scored a third Brewers run off a fielding error in the fourth.

Frelick tied the score when he led off the bottom of the sixth with his 408-foot solo shot off relief pitcher Ian Seymour. Pratt returned for his go-ahead RBI single in the seventh off Tyler Wells.

Bullpen arms JoJo Romero, Dustin May, DL Hall, Abner Uribe and Aaron Ashby combined to allow just four hits and no runs over the final six innings.

"As long as there's game left, we have a chance," Pratt said. "I think we've all bought into that."

The Rays threatened with a final base runner in the top of the ninth, but Ashby cemented the triumph with a game-ending strikeout of Diaz.

"It was just about making pitches," Ashby said.

Brewers right-handed pitcher Logan Henderson allowed three hits and four runs, including three earned, over the first three frames. Rasmussen allowed six hits and three runs over 3 2/3 innings.

Frelick, Contreras and left fielder Jackson Chourio collected two hits apiece for the Brewers. Center fielder Jonny DeLuca, who went 2 for 4, was the only Rays player to log more than one hit.

The Rays (0-2) will host the Brewers (2-0) in Game 3 of the best-of-seven game series at 8 p.m. EDT Monday at Tropicana Field in St. Petersburg, Fla.. They will host Game 4 at the same time there Tuesday.

articles.title: World Series game ends on controversial check-swing strikeout
articles.summary: Yandy Diaz's strikeout to end Game 2 involved a controversial call.
articles.body:
For the second night in a row, the final out of a World Series game involved some drama.

With a runner on third and two outs in the ninth inning on Saturday in Game 2, first base umpire James Hoye ruled that the Tampa Bay Rays ' Yandy Diaz was unable to hold his swing on a third strike from Milwaukee Brewers lefty Aaron Ashby.

Home plate umpire Jim Wolf initially didn't think that Diaz had gone around, but Brewers catcher William Contreras won his appeal to first. The strikeout ended the Brewers' 5-4 win at American Family Field in Milwaukee, overcoming a four-run deficit against Tampa Bay .

Diaz's check-swing was one of the closer calls you'll see in baseball, as the rulebook lacks a rigid, black-and-white definition.

articles.summary: A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85. Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23.
articles.body:
A knife-wielding man was arrested Friday night for threatening crew members on the Brooklyn set of Miami Vice ‘85 .

Citing information from the NYPD, TMZ reports that a police officer working security on the set arrested Alex Perez, 23, who has a criminal record.

“Perez can be seen being escorted off the set by a staffer before taking out the large knife from his sweatshirt pocket,” according to TMZ, which also posted a video of the incident .

“A cop on the scene then arrested Perez -- who hurled the n-word at the production staff member while in cuffs -- at 11:17 PM.”

The site reports that Perez has been charged with menacing with a weapon in the 2nd degree and criminal possession of a weapon in the 4th degree.

Miami Vice ‘85 has been filming in New York this week, including scenes featuring Michael B. Jordan and John Leguizamo in that appear to faithfully recreate the opening moments of the original TV series’ pilot.

Director Joseph Kosinski’s film is inspired by the series’ two-part pilot (“ Brother’s Keeper ”) and the show’s first season in general.

For more on Miami Vice ‘85, check out these first look images of Jordan and Austin Butler in costume as detectives Ricardo Tubbs and Sonny Crockett, respectively.

articles.title: Another Brewers comeback win has fans fired up on social media
articles.summary: Social media reacted strongly to the Milwaukee Brewers' second World Series win.

The Milwaukee Brewers are two wins away from their first World Series championship.

Milwaukee's comeback kids dug out of a 4-0 first-inning hole to beat the Tampa Bay Rays , 5-4, in Game 2 of the World Series on Saturday night, Oct. 24, at American Family Field.

articles.title: Si no sabes qué hacer este Halloween, tengo el plan perfecto para ti: cuatro juegos de mesa perfectos para amigos o familia
articles.standfirst: Si este año prefieres quedarte en casa y darle un toque diferente a La Noche de Brujas, estos cuatro juegos de mesa pueden ser justo lo que estás buscando.
articles.summary: Si este año prefieres quedarte en casa y darle un toque diferente a La Noche de Brujas, estos cuatro juegos de mesa pueden ser justo lo que estás buscando.
articles.body: Halloween. La Noche de Brujas. El Día de Todos los Santos. El 31 de octubre de cada año somos muchos los que celebramos la noche más terrorífica del año de muy diversas maneras. Los hay quienes prefieren salir a tomar algo. También los que gustan de disfrutar de una buena sesión de cine o videojuegos. O los que prefieren pasar una jornada más tranquila junto a un libro de terror. Hay muchas opciones, aunque hay una de la que yo disfruto especialmente en un día como este: una noche de juegos de mesa de terror y/o que respiren la atmósfera de tan señalado momento. Si tuviese que destacar alguno para empezar, ese tendría que ser Mysterium. Y no porque sea mejor o peor que los demás —todos son muy buenos, de eso que no quede duda—, sino porque es uno de a los que más horas le he dedicado. Halloween o no, Mysterium es uno de mis preferidos, y lo es porque me obliga a meterme en la cabeza de los demás... o a que los demás se metan en la mía. Recuerda a Dixit, pero en un ambiente de misterios esotéricos. En Mysterium, un jugador interpreta a un fantasma que no puede hablar y el resto, a un grupo de médiums que deben descubrir un asesinato. Más concretamente, dónde ocurrió, qué arma se utilizó y quién fue. El sistema es sencillo: el espíritu envía mensajes mediante un número determinado (varía según la dificultad) de cartas con dibujos abstractos a modo de pistas. Es un juego de equipo, así que intentará que acierten. Los médiums, por su parte, tendrán que intentar descubrir qué les está intentando decir, escogiendo entre diferentes posibilidades para ir determinando en orden tanto el lugar como el arma y el asesino. Cada médium tendrá su propia ruta y, una vez se hayan resuelto todas, habrá que dilucidar quién es el verdadero asesino de entre todos los sospechosos. El siguiente juego del que me gustaría hablar es menos de pensar y más de actuar. Se trata de Zombie Burrito, el Balón prisionero de la Noche de Brujas. Es uno de los juegos más sencillos y, al mismo tiempo, de los más divertidos de este artículo. La premisa es sencilla: los jugadores se tienen que dividir en dos equipos diferentes y bombardear al otro a burritazos. Y no, no os preocupéis: no duele. Es otro juego al que he jugado también mucho y hacerse daño con el burrito es imposible, porque es de espuma, está acolchado y es muy blando. El juego se desarrolla por rondas. En cada una, se van pasando cartas por una mesa y nuestro objetivo es juntar 3 iguales lo más rápido posible. La gracia es que las cartas tienen efectos especiales. Por ejemplo, hay algunas que desencadenan directamente una guerra de burritos, mientras que otras pueden darte ventaja durante la ronda. La gracia de Zombie Burrito es que te obliga a estar en movimiento, por lo que, si prefieres algo más movido, es una gran opción. Mi tercera recomendación es un clásico entre clásicos. Exploding Kittens es uno de los juegos más populares y laureados de los últimos años, por lo que no es raro que tenga un buen puñado de versiones. Zombie Kittens es una de ellas y no, no hace falta el juego original para jugar: es totalmente independiente, por lo que se puede disfrutar de él de manera individual. Lo que más me gusta de este es que le da una vuelta de tuerca a su predecesor, ya que aquí la muerte no es el final. En Exploding Kittens, tu objetivo es ser el último en pie mientras juegas diferentes cartas. En Zombie Kittens, la muerte es solo otra mecánica, puesto que los jugadores que caen en partida pueden seguir liándola desde la tumba e incluso volver a la vida. Es un juego que destaca para quienes busquen algo rápido, directo y con un toque algo más gamberro. Gusta del humor negro y no se anda con tonterías, pero sin llegar a ser excesivo en ningún momento. Se aprende a jugar enseguida y las partidas son muy dinámicas. Además, es el típico juego que te insta a seguir dándole caña. Pica bastante y te saca tu lado más competitivo con facilidad. Para terminar, otro juego al que le he dedicado bastantes horas de mi vida: Espíritu... ¿Estás ahí? En este juego de mesa viajaremos directamente a un castillo encantado en plena noche de Halloween. Es un título que suelo disfrutar mucho porque te obliga a interactuar con el resto de los jugadores, siendo un título de los que buscan potenciar la sensación de inmersión ludonarrativa. En Espíritu... ¿Estás ahí? tendremos que descubrir quién se esconde detrás de cada disfraz, buscando entre humanos y criaturas de la noche que intentan pasar desapercibidas. La mecánica gira en torno a las cartas de personaje y de acción, que permiten investigar, poner a prueba a los demás y tratar de desenmascarar a quienes no son lo que parecen. Lo interesante es que no basta con fijarse en las cartas que tienes delante: también hay que prestar atención a lo que hacen los demás y desconfiar de quienes podrían estar intentando engañarte. Además, cuenta con tres modos de juego diferentes, por lo que ofrece varias maneras de enfrentarse a una misma idea. Puedes centrarte en descubrir las identidades ocultas, jugar por equipos enfrentando al bien y al mal o probar un modo en el que cada uno debe sobrevivir por su cuenta. Y hasta aquí nuestras recomendaciones para una noche de juegos de mesa en Halloween, tanto para los más peques como para los más adultos.

articles.title: Así se ve la 'armada española' en NBA 2K27: Los rookies se estrenan con este impresionante parecido
articles.standfirst: El videojuego reproducía físicamente a los nuestros casi a la perfección
articles.summary: El videojuego reproducía físicamente a los nuestros casi a la perfección
articles.body: La NBA ya ha empezado y los fans del baloncesto lo celebramos. Pero este año, a diferencia de muchos otros recientemente, los españoles estamos especialmente pendientes porque la 'armada española' que hay en la NBA nos ilusiona y mucho. Y es que Santi Aldama y Hugo González ya no estarán solo para llevar nuestra bandera por los pabellones de la liga de baloncesto más importante del planeta. A los de Dallas y Boston se han añadido tres jugadores que durante la Summer League, la pretemporada y este inicio de temporada ya están dando mucho de qué hablar. Sobre todo Aday Mara, el pívot que llegaba a Oklahoma en el pick 12 y que es, sin duda, el que más está sorprendiendo en Estados Unidos, y el tapón a Wembanyama en su debut es el ejemplo. Pero además llegaban Baba Miller, el que ya va contando con minutos en los Clippers pese a ser un pick de segunda ronda, siendo importante en los minutos que tiene en pista gracias a esa coordinación, tamaño y potencia, y Sergio de Larrea, el que comparte equipo con Aldama en Dallas y que también, aunque con pocos minutos de momento, puede ser una pieza clave para organizar el juego de los Mavericks. Pues bien, antes de que arrancara la temporada real de la NBA, la virtual ya había dado el 'pistoletazo de salida', ya que NBA 2K27 lleva ya semanas entre nosotros. Y como ya estamos viendo cómo les está yendo a los españoles sobre las pistas de la NBA, vamos a ver cómo son en el videojuego. Y es que un año más NBA 2K hace una labor increíble a la hora de plasmar físicamente a los jugadores en el juego y los españoles son un ejemplo. Quizá Santi y Sergio son a los que más pegas podemos poner, pero Hugo, Baba y Aday parecen una fotografía en movimiento.

articles.title: Magic: The Gathering's Top 12 Most Powerful Commander Precons Of All Time
articles.summary: Looking for Magic's most powerful boxed precon decks for Commander? Here's our top 12, including Universes Beyond.
articles.body:
Magic: The Gathering is a fantastic card game, but the Commander format has given it even more legs.

It revolves around a central Commander that helms your deck, giving it a ton of personality as players gravitate towards their favorite legendary creatures to build around.

Wizards of the Coast finally recognized the format in 2011, beginning a deluge of preconstructed decks that are playable right out of the box. We’ve got a full list of them , but for now, we’ve narrowed down our top 12.

These aren’t presented in any real order, but let us know which ones you’ve played!

The Most Powerful Magic: The Gathering Commander Precons

The Ur-Dragon still commands a high fee, and the 10/10 standard-bearer of this five-color precon is a beneficiary of the Eminence keyword. It drops the cost of Dragon spells by 1 mana, and then, when it is on the field, your dragons essentially multiply as they attack.

It’s far and away the most powerful preconstructed Dragon deck, but if you’re looking for cheaper alternatives, my first deck was Draconic Destruction from the Commander starter decks, and Temur Roar is a great three-color dragon deck with upgrade potential, too.

Counter Blitz - Universes Beyond: Final Fantasy

All the Final Fantasy decks were great, but Counter Blitz stands ahead of the others for the counter-switching shenanigans it could lead to.

Tidus, Yuna’s Guardian, lets you move counters around, but the type of counter isn’t specified. There are four Summon creatures in the deck that you could essentially keep around forever with the right counter shuffling.

The deck also contains some great reprints, like Three Visits and Farewell, while Yuna is a great Commander in her own right.

Necron Dynasties - Universes Beyond: Warhammer 40K

This mono-black Warhammer deck costs a pretty penny these days, with its Commander, Szarekh, able to mill cards to put more creatures into your hand.

Personally, I prefer to use Imotekh the Stormlord as my Commander, though, letting you create token creatures as you use recursion and power up a creature during combat.

Out of the Tombs is awesome, too. It lets you risk milling yourself out, but can give you a whole host of board presence in the late game. Better yet, this deck is expected to be reprinted soon .

Mutant Menace - Universes Beyond: Fallout

I hate this deck . It’s a pain to deal with, causing plenty of mill and life loss for the whole table, but there’s no denying it’s effective.

The Wise Mothman, its Commander, dishes out rad counters and then grows in power as those counters mill cards and wound your opponents.

Strong, the Brutish Thespian, can even add life from radiation, making a great mechanic (at least for you), even more useful.

A deck that’s so effective at dealing damage it can make Commander matches take half as long to complete, Endless Punishment is a great deck that gets even better if you swap out Valgavoth with Master of Pain.

This 5/5 stops opponents from gaining life, has Menace, and turns the mana cost of every first spell of a player’s turn into damage against another player. Given how expensive spells get as the match wears on, that can be a big, big hit.

Reprints of Vial Smasher the Fierce and Witch’s Clinic were welcome, too. You can also score Endless Punishment as part of the Duskmourn Commander Deck bundle at Amazon , which is currently down to $189.20 for four decks (dropping from $242.97) .

Sliver Swarm, as the name suggests, is a deck that’s all about Slivers , a creature type that’s relatively minor on its own but buffs every other ally with the same type.

This five-color precon is a problem for everyone at the table, helmed by the Sliver Gravemother that can help bring cards back from the graveyard as attacking tokens. Oh, and it means you can have multiple copies of Legendary creatures, too.

The deck had fewer reprints than some, but it’s powerful - and ripe for upgrades if you can find some extra Slivers.

A colorless Eldrazi deck , this one puts Zhulodok, Void Gorger as your Commander and lets you enjoy double Cacade on spells with mana value 7 or higher - ouch.

Kozilek, the Great Distortion, is another Legendary Creature you can pick as your Commander. It costs a lot, but acts as a 12/12 with Menace and facilitates card draw.

It That Betrays was an awesome reprint, and I recently managed to find one myself to put in my Eldrazi Incursion upgrade (more on that later).

There’s a reason that Edgar Markov remains the de facto vampire-type Commander in Magic: The Gathering. His Eminence ability, which triggers even if he’s in the Command Zone, means this 4/4 with First Strike and haste can create Vampire tokens as you cast spells of that type, and he empowers them with +1/+1 when he attacks.

Teferi’s Protection is here, too, with this being the kind of deck with no real weaknesses that’s easy to pilot as well.

Food and Fellowship - Universes Beyond: Lord of the Rings

The Lord of the Rings Commander Decks were all solid, but Food and Fellowship wins out for its strength in just about every aspect. Sam generates Food tokens to gain life, then Frodo is tempted by the Ring as you consume them, with each of the Partner cards feeding into a cycle.

It’s not all Shire-friendly, either, with some true wrath coming in the form of Toxic Deluge, spot removal like Path to Exile and Swords to Plowshares, and cards like The Gaffer to turn that lifegain into more card draw. A great, well-constructed deck.

Veloci-Ramp-Tor - Lost Caverns of Ixalan

The kind of deck that steamrolls many of the precons in recent years, Pantlaza, Sun-Favored helms this dinosaur offering and helps you bring more and more creatures into play with the Discover ability.

With cards like Wakening Sun’s Avatar being a non-dino board wipe and comically large beasts like Apex Altisaur, this deck is wild right out of the box.

Party Time - Commander Legends: Battle for Baldur’s Gate

This Baldur’s Gate-flavored deck’s commander, Nalia de-Arnise, is a low-cost 3/3 that lets you case Cleric, Rogue, Warrior, and Wizard spells from the top of your library.

It really doesn’t take long to build up a formidable force in early turns, letting you get a head start while your opponents are scrambling to find blockers. The deck is pretty expensive now, though.

A chaotic deck that can be built in multiple ways, Multiverse Reforged is helmed by Jace, Multiverse Architect. The ideal scenario here is to build up a bunch of tokens and then polymorph them into some of the deck's bigger threats, like the Ur-Sphinx, Ob Nixilis, the Ascended, and Darksteel Angel.

One of the best parts of this deck is that it includes a bunch of alternate versions of some of Magic's most iconic cards, like the exceptionally powerful Dack Fayden, Helping Hand and Avacyn, Angel of Horror.

The following might not be the most powerful, but I’ve enjoyed playing with them.

Heavenly Inferno is one of the first Commander precons, and its strength lies in its flexibility. The Commander, Kaalia of the Vast, helps you bring creatures into play, whether they’re Angels, Demons, or Dragons.

Because of that, you can easily swap out a bunch of Angels and Demons for Dragons, or lean into two of them if you’d prefer. As with some others on this list, it can get out of hand pretty swiftly, and while there are a bunch of cards in here that can be swiftly removed because they don't fall into the relevant types, Kaalia remains fun to build around.

An Eldrazi deck with five colors and a Commander that can copy spells and activated abilities for two generic mana, Eldrazi Incursion is great off the bat, but becomes positively vile with the right upgrades.

It’s probably not a deck for newcomers, though, because the sheer volume of triggers can feel overwhelming.

Tyranid Swarm - Universes Beyond: Warhammer 40K

I’ve had games that have been won because my Haruspex has gained so much power that it deals huge damage to opponents, or converted its power to mana for a big late-game push.

Magus Lucea Kane’s doubling up of X-cost spells, and the Swarmlord turning your creatures with counters into card draw, means there are some really fun strategies here - Tyranid Swarm is a deck that truly does feel like a ‘swarm’, and can give you big creatures to attack with, and plenty of tokens back to defend if you’re smart.

Riders of Rohan - Universes Beyond: Lord of The Rings

It might not be the flashiest deck since it relies on an awful lot of Human Knights in battles between Eldrazi monstrosities, Dragons, and spellcasters, but Riders of Rohan is a precon that’s very well put together.

Aside from a weakness against flying, it’s able to mobilize an army with frightening speed, and it grows with your aggression. I’ve seen it pop off many, many times, and it’s always something to behold.

Explorers of the Deep - Lost Caverns of Ixalan

This Simic (Blue/Green) deck is helmed by Hakbal of the Surging Soul, and uses the Explore mechanic to great effect, either ramping your lands, netting you creatures, or getting card draw.

It’s a Commander with a ton of value (I’m looking to squeeze him into another underwater-themed deck as we speak), but there’s also Kindred Discovery in the deck as well to get even more card draw from your Merfolk.

There’s something about flipping cards face-up to surprise an opponent that feels very Yu-Gi-Oh, and I love Jump Scare (!) for that very reason.

Being able to flip a 15/15 Worldspine Wurm up is a great party trick, but there are other great cards in here like Ashaya, Soul of the Wild, and Aesi, Tyrant of Gyre Strait. Just like Endless Punishment, Jump Scare! is also discounted as part of the Duskmourn Commander Deck bundle at Amazon , which is currently down to $189.20 for four decks (dropping from $242.97) .

Many of these decks are tricky to get your hands on thanks to limited printings, but there are some solid entrants from the Class of 2026.

Will these be remembered as fondly in the years to come? It's hard to say, but here are four decks we can recommend right now.

A five-color precon all about Elemental creatures, Dance of the Elements isn't ideal for newcomers because it's all centered around ETB triggers and those can get out of hand swiftly.

Ashling, the Limitless, uses evoke to get big creatures out cheaper, and when they're sacrificed because of it, you can create a copy that costs you mana to keep around. If you'd prefer, Mass of Mysteries is a fun backup Commander that gives a lot of your creatures the myriad keyword so they attack around the table.

Secrets of Strixhaven came with five really fun precons, but Lorehold Spirit is arguably the best, incentivizing you to remove cards from your graveyard to build a spirit army.

Amassing all of those apparitions is particularly useful with the face Commander, Quintorius, History Chaser. This Planeswalker can give them all double strike and vigilance, meaning a big, game-ending swing.

Another offering from Secrets of Strixhaven, Witherbloom Pestilence is all about sacrificng cards to power up other creatures, and in Dina, Essence Brewer, it has a one-card engine to do both with relative ease.

Gyome, Master Chef is a nice inclusion as a sought-after reprint, as is Nether Traitor, and there are essentially a bunch of great cards to slot into any deck with access to green, black, or both.

Universes Beyond continues to divide the Magic: The Gathering community, but this Avengers-themed deck is pretty solid.

It plays off of hero synergies, whether you've got Captain America being buffed as they enter, or Nick Fury reducing their cost, and is remarkably easy to play with.

Counter Intelligence/World Shaper - Edge of Eternities

OK, I’m cheating a little here, but both Edge of Eternities decks were great. Counter Intelligence is helmed by Kilo, Apogee Mind, and ramps up counters swiftly by proliferating every time it’s turned sideways.

World Shaper , on the other hand, is a deck I’ve had a lot of fun with. Szarel, Genesis Shepherd lets you play lands from your graveyard, and there are a ton of landfall effects that play into that, too.

Lloyd Coombes is an experienced freelancer in tech, gaming and fitness seen at Polygon, Eurogamer, Macworld, TechRadar and many more. He's a big fan of Magic: The Gathering and other collectible card games, much to his wife's dismay.

articles.title: Angel Reese explains what went wrong for her in eight-point display in Game 4  loss
articles.summary: The WNBA Finals are all tied up at 2-2. Angel Reese spoke after the Game 4 disappointment about what didn’t work for her.
articles.body:
The WNBA Finals are all tied up at 2-2. Angel Reese spoke after the Game 4 disappointment about what didn't work for her.

After Game 2 and Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, it looked like a foregone conclusion that Angel Reese would be the Finals MVP. Atlanta had taken a 2-1 lead with one more game on their home floor, and were one win away from taking a commanding lead in the Finals.

The Valkyries had other plans, though. They bounced back from their 26-point Game 3 defeat with a 67-62 win. Gabby Williams led the way for her team with a 17-point display. More importantly, they stopped Reese from going off after two consecutive monster games. The Dream star spoke about her bad night.

Angel Reese says she rushed her shots and didn't 'take her time' like the last two games

The Dream struggled to find their rhythm offensively, with Angel held to just eight points on 2-of-12 shooting. Rhyne Howard had a great game, but it wasn't enough for Atlanta to get the win they needed. Reese took accountability after the game.

Adjusting within a series is what leads to playoff success in basketball. This is true for the teams and the individual superstars. Change begins with recognising mistakes, and Reese was upfront about what she got wrong in Game 4.

"I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn't take my time and finish around the basket like I've been doing in the last 3 games," Reese told media at the press conference. It happens and I'm just looking forward to the next game and I'll just be better.

The straightforward statement from Angel is another sign of her maturity as a WNBA star. It is now effectively a best-of-3 contest between the two teams for the championship. Reese has shown enough during these playoffs that fans will have complete trust in the superstar.

articles.title: Rumored Lucia Actress Goes Viral After Dodging Swarm of GTA 6 Comments During Livestream
articles.summary: Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6, has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.
articles.body:
Manni L. Perez, the actress long rumored to be playing Lucia in GTA 6 , has gone viral after dodging a swarm of comments from Grand Theft Auto fans during a recent livestream.

Rockstar Games has refrained from confirming the vast majority of the cast of next month's new GTA game, but as if there was ever any doubt, that hasn't stopped ravenous fans from piecing a list together themselves. Perez is one name theorists have talked about for years, so she took a few minutes to let thousands of viewers get to know her while masterfully dodging a swarm of GTA 6 comments along the way.

Reaching a peak of more than 2,100 viewers on a six-month-old Instagram account with just nine posts, Perez spent her 12-minute livestream just talking about her life growing up in a "small, rural, redneck-y" town. She lives in a studio apartment with a dog, loves to cook, grew up driving trucks, and as far as everyone else is officially concerned, she definitely will not be the star of the so-called biggest video game of all time in a little less than a month.

"But yeah, no, I'm not rich. I'm a regular person," Perez said when responding to fans who assumed she was wealthy. "I live in a small studio apartment, which I love. I have my tiny, little itty-bitty kitchen, and it's just me and my dog. I do everything on my own, and I've done everything on my own for a very long time, and I love it, and I'm very grateful. I have a family that loves me, and I'm just feeling like I'm in a really good place, where I am in my life."

"I want a green truck," she said with a smile while ignoring the horde comments mentioning "Lucia" and "GTA 6." Some responded that, no, actually, she doesn't live alone, because she has Jason to keep her company. Others were subtler, asking if she'll be playing Rockstar's latest or if she's just "ready for next month." Despite the steady flow of responses begging her to confirm her alleged role – which would be guarded under a strict non-disclosure agreement, even if it were real – Perez only acknowledged users commenting about anything else.

Keep in mind that this all comes from years of clues gathered by fans, but Rockstar's lack of confirmation doesn't mean there's nothing to suggest Perez is playing Lucia in GTA 6. As others have highlighted , the actress has a history of live-action and voice roles. She has credits for single episodes of shows like Jessica Jones, The Blacklist, and Law & Order: Special Victims Unit. Funnily enough, she also played a blackjack dealer in Grand Theft Auto Online.

Her place in Rockstar history may be given a bump when GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S next month, November 19. If you're wondering who might be playing Lucia's partner in crime, Jason, fans have long speculated that Modern Family and Grey's Anatomy actor Dylan Rourke filled the role, but he, too, has yet to be confirmed.

Who has been confirmed, whether Rockstar and any likely NDAs like it or not, is Stephen Root, who said he will be seen playing drug trafficker Brian Heder . Otherwise, we might need to wait until launch to see the full cast, so don't go sending messages to any actors just yet.

Fans may have tracked down the voice actors behind one of the biggest game launches of all time, but it's par for the course when it comes to Grand Theft Auto players. One fan spent three months charting planetary positions just to try and learn when trailer 3 would premiere (they were wrong). Another fan measured oxygen levels to try and achieve the same feat (they, too, were wrong).

Either way, GTA 6 marketing is continuing to ramp up . While we wait these last few precious weeks, you can see why some fans are expecting a sweep at The Game Awards 2026 . You can also learn more about the love and care Rockstar put into its new video game , but don't forget to read up on IGN's interview .

articles.title: This Switch 2 sequel accessory was a few millimeters away from being good
articles.summary: Crkd’s $99.99 Nitro Deck 2 is a solid controller accessory for the Nintendo Switch and Switch 2, but its button and stick layout isn’t comfortable.
articles.body: The Crkd Nitro Deck was a saving grace for the original Nintendo Switch. The slide-on $59.99 accessory brought Hall effect sticks to drift-plagued consoles — no need to open up your Joy-Con for a complicated repair. The Nitro Deck 2, made for both the original Switch and the larger Switch 2, continues the tradition of having better sticks than what Nintendo puts in even the newest Joy-Con (though these aren’t Hall effect or TMR). But it doesn’t feel as essential, and there’s one thing I really can’t stand about it. It’s too difficult to use the Nitro Deck 2’s ABXY face buttons without the right stick getting in the way. The stick-to-button arrangement is a big step down from the original Nitro Deck (and especially bad compared with the symmetrical Steam Deck-like stick layout in the video output-ready Nitro Deck Plus). I’m surprised Crkd’s team thought this was an improvement. My patience with the run-based gameplay in Echo Weaver is already tested enough, and trying to quickly hammer inputs on the Deck 2 only adds to the frustration. [Image: [Image: Your preference may differ, but I like having a little breathing room between the right stick and the face buttons. Some companies choose to space them out or, in the case of the Switch 2’s Joy-Con, make the stick small enough to allow my thumb to hover over it so I can press the buttons. The Deck 2 makes me adjust my thumb’s angle of approach outside of what’s comfortable. It’s just a few millimeters off. The original’s superior slide-in design was traded for a vice-grip design to ensure compatibility with both the newer and older Switch consoles. The Deck 2 has a twisting mechanism on the back that you can loosen, tighten, or lock. It’s clever, though the tradeoff for broader compatibility is a design that feels inherently less secure. Crkd is asking Switch 2 owners to put a ton of faith in this mechanism staying tight around their $500 consoles. My Switch 2 didn’t feel wobbly during testing, but I’d rather not have to think about its safety at all when I’m gaming. I would have preferred a slide-in design for the Deck 2 made expressly for the Switch 2. [Image: [Image: It’s disappointing that Crkd’s Joy-Con-replacing solution isn’t as good because I like some things about it more than the original. For instance, the accessory has adjustable tension on both sticks, so they can snap back to their original position faster or slower than the default speed. Also, the accessory’s bulkier design makes the console more comfortable in my medium-size hands to use in handheld mode. It also has a bunch of customizable buttons: four on its back and an extra near the triggers. Not many similar accessories are out there yet, and the other one I tried (the abxylute N6) wasn’t all that good, either. I plan to test Mobapad’s latest take on Joy-Con soon, and it seems promising. Alternatively, you can add a bunch of comfort to your Switch 2 in handheld mode with either the Dbrand Killswitch 2 or the Mechanism Basecase. And with the money left over, you could buy a good wireless Switch 2 controller with long-lasting sticks and better rumble. [Product: Crkd Nitro Deck 2 | Photography by Cameron Faulkner / The Verge

articles.title: Mass Effect Leaks Reveal Canceled BioWare Game's Story Would Have Accounted for 'All' Choices From Previous Games
articles.summary: Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.
articles.body:
Additional details about BioWare's canceled Mass Effect game have leaked online, revealing a story that would have taken choices from the Commander Shepard trilogy into account if EA hadn't shut down the studio.

The long-awaited and currently canned follow-up for the sci-fi RPG franchise, which was working under the title Mass Effect: Universe, was built around decisions made in the original games, according to comments shared by former technical director Romain Toutain during a recent livestream (via Kotaku ). As more details about the project leak, there's no telling exactly how thorough this system would have been, but he did his best to give fans an idea.

"All the choices made in the first Mass Effect games were taken into account," Toutain said (translation via Bluesky user @loustica-lucia.bsky.social ). "One of the reasons why it was called 'Mass Effect: Universe' is that you had so many choices. That you could plug your saves together to create parallel universes, to keep it simple. It's not exactly how it worked. You had different timelines, basically."

Mass Effect fans know how crucial the series' overarching story is, especially when it comes to Commander Shepard's first three installments in his/her fight against the Reapers. Outside of the ill-fated Andromeda follow-up that launched in 2017, players were able to carry major choices from each entry over to the next, resulting in a trilogy of games with a highly personalized story.

Relationships, major character deaths, and even the fate of an entire species are just a few of the ways Shepard can be steered to shape the galaxy, and although whether it was all worth it in the end is still up for debate, it seems Mass Effect: Universe would have offered an opportunity to right some wrongs . Toutain said they had plans for those who just prefer to experiment with the story and its many, many branches, too. He likened the freedom to "generate timelines" to Spike Chunsoft's 2016 video game, Zero Time Dilemma .

"You have no f**king idea just how great it was," he continued. Then, responding to a fan asking whether Mass Effect: Universe would have featured systems similar to what was found in Dragon Age: Inquisition and the series' lore-tailoring Keep application, he said, "kinda, yeah."

"It's more like, you can make decisions that might contradict things you've already done or thing you have to do, and so it would create plot 'points' in the timeline. I mean, that was the theory. It worked, in practice. I'll tell you about the tech one day because it was really exciting.

"We got worked up, f**k. Everything in the game. Everything was stateful, and at any time, you could stop the game – I mean you could pause it – and ask a system that solved logical equations, 'Is this valid?' And if it isn't valid, what conditions must be met for it to be valid?"

The ideas Toutain teased sound ambitious and complex, and unfortunately, they will likely never see the light of day. EA announced last week that it had shuttered the long-running RPG developer and canceled what would likely have been called Mass Effect: Universe , with additional plans for the franchise's future in games on hold, too. Fans have already erected a #SaveMassEffect movement in the aftermath, with a petition garnering an unreal 185,000 signatures at the time of this story's publication.

11 Mass Effect Characters and Moments the TV Show Needs to Be a Hit

Other highlights from Toutain's stream include the revelation that the Reaper-like hand featured in recently leaked footage was named Billy, as well as the idea that the developers were hoping to craft a story that gave each player a completely unique experience. More information about what Mass Effect 5 would have been have also leaked in the days after BioWare's demise. Those details include a full trailer , as well as gameplay details that promised missions with "Hitman-style freedom." The Prime Video show, meanwhile, is said to still be in the works .

articles.title: Clayface Looks Like a Win for the DCU After Earning $43 Million in Box Office Opening Weekend
articles.summary: Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.
articles.body:
Clayface looks set up to be a win for the DCU after securing the top spot at the box office with an estimated global haul of $43 million.

It's a strong start for the low-budget DCU film, split between $24 million domestically and $19 million internationally. The opening weekend total falls toward the higher end of early projections as audiences showed up to see Tom Rhys Harries bring a twisted and often overlooked Batman villain to the big screen.

With brutal body horror elements in a story that sees the birth of its titular character, Clayface follows Matt Hagen as he attempts to rebuild his life after a horrible attack leaves his face scarred. Starring Harries, directed by James Watkins, and written by Mike Flanagan and Hossein Amini, this latest DCU movie took viewers into the darkest corners of James Gunn and Peter Safran's universe they've seen yet, with a pretty hard-R rating.

It's for these reasons that the DCU's foray into a new live-action Gotham City left fans with question marks as they feared how a more adult-oriented story could fit into the same world as something as bubbly and bright as 2025's Superman. So far, at least, it seems to have paid off, at least compared to Supergirl , which landed as a dud in the DCU earlier this year.

The Milly Alcock-led superhero movie was deemed a box office bomb after it premiered in June. That's mostly due to its almost $200 million budget, which towered over the comparatively measly $126.46 million it gathered throughout its run (via Box Office Mojo ). Clayface, on the other hand, is starting its time in theaters almost matching the $44 million budget reported by Variety .

Although there is certainly plenty of ground to cover before officially being declared a success, it seems like a strong start. A few factors will help carry Clayface throughout the rest of its run: Firstly, its October release timing means Halloween moviegoers will have something spooky to watch next weekend. Reviews have been pretty solid, too, with Rotten Tomatoes recording a 75% from critics and 94% from audiences.

Gunn, at least, is proud of Matt Hagen's live-action introduction in the DCU. As viewers went to theaters to squirm at Clayface's backstory, movie fan surveyor site CinemaScore polled an "A-" from audiences. It's a feat rarely seen in the horror genre, something the DC Studios co-chairman made sure to note in a post on Threads .

"Really proud of this," Gunn said. "Sinners is the only horror movie to have EVER gotten an A CinemaScore, and only three horror movies have gotten an A- in the last couple years – Obsession, Weapons, and, now, Clayface. As always, all praise goes to James, Mike, Hossein, Tom, Naomi and the whole gang."

Clayface is in good company in the horror world and in its opening weekend. Coming in second, domestically, was Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim's Elizabeth Holmes documentary, You Can See Everything . After a limited launch drew rave reviews and positive earnings last weekend, the three-hour movie returned for its second bout with an additional $19.5 million. That's a 25% increase from its debut, driven by wider availability across an additional 1,800 theaters in the market.

Strong word-of-mouth could see the Fielder picture continue to attract viewers in the coming weeks as moviegoers dare to dip their toes into Holmes' world and the story of Theranos. Stop-motion studio Laika, meanwhile, might be in for a rough time. Its latest claymation feature, a fantasy epic directed by Travis Knight called Wildwood , came in third at the domestic box office with $11.77 million. That's above projections for the Coraline moviemaker but still far, far below its reported budget of $100 million.

Though still well above 2019's Missing Link, Wildwood's opening weekend numbers put it toward the lower end of debuts in the studio's history, too. Those who have seen Laika's latest might be surprised to hear it could struggle to recoup costs, as Laika has managed to pull some remarkably strong reviews so far. Rotten Tomatoes shows it with a 100% from critics and 97% from audiences. We here at IGN gave it an 8/10 , calling it an "arresting, exciting fantasy epic made all the more impressive by the fact that it's handmade and hand-animated."

Other box office highlights as we approach Halloween are Street Fighter , which brought another $16.8 million worldwide in its second weekend. Alexander Skarsgård and Olivia Colman's Wicker had a domestic total of $5.75 million in its more limited first weekend.

For more on the biggest movies of the weekend, you can read IGN's 7/10 Clayface review . You can also read why we thought You Can See Everything is a 10/10 . If you caught the new DCU flick in theaters – or if you didn't becuase you're a bit squeamish – you can see our breakdown of its ending here .

articles.title: Derry SFC: 'It's probably been too long' - Magherafelt's Odhran Lynch on title
articles.summary: Magherafelt goalkeeper Odhran Lynch says its "probably been too long" after this club beat three-in-a-row chasing Newbridge to win a first Derry SFC title since 2019.
articles.body:
Magherafelt goalkeeper Odhran Lynch says it has "probably been too long" after this club beat three-in-a-row chasing Newbridge to win a first Derry SFC title since 2019.

Goals from Johnny McErlain, Aidan McCluskey and Cormac Murphy sealed the 3-17 to 0-20 victory at Celtic Park.

The south Derry club were beaten in three finals since their last victory seven years ago, when Lynch was just 19 years of age in a victory over Glen, but he now savours the victories even more.

"It's just nice to get back and it's probably been too long," Lynch told BBC Sport NI.

"We've been knocking on the door and that's the fourth time coming into a final since we last won it.

"We just made everything hard for ourselves. We probably still made things hard for ourselves there today, but it's just great to get over the line."

Lynch admits, after winning the trophy as a teenager in 2019, that "you're sitting there going and thinking we're going to be there every year".

"But the following year we're in the relegation play-off.

"It's just sticking at it. The young boys that have come through there have been awesome, they just bring a whole different buzz."

Lynch has had his struggles with injury in recent season as he missed out on playing for both club and county Derry, which made the return to fitness and the successes even more special.

He also paid tribute to club coach Gavin Devlin, who aided his recovery off and on the field, even while guiding Louth to the All-Ireland semi-final as manager.

"It's 363 days since I had the operation on the hip, so a year on Tuesday. It was well over a year before I got to play any football again. It's unbelievable.

"I've played 13 or 14 games in a row. I haven't been beat since I've come back thankfully, in the league or Championship.

"I was out of hospital and I was home three or four days. He [Devlin] was lifting me every day to go for a coffee and go to the gym to do rehab," Lynch continued.

"I couldn't even get in and out of the car really. He was lifting my leg in and out for me. That's what he's doing. He's Louth manager and he's a club man too.

"It's just unbelievable, you have the right people there looking after you. It makes it even better when you win something."

articles.title: X-Men Actor Christopher Abbott Insists His Professor X Is Not in Doomsday or Secret Wars
articles.summary: Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.
articles.body:
Professor X actor Christopher Abbott said Marvel fans won't see him in Avengers: Doomsday or Secret Wars because he needs to wrap up his time with X-Men before doing any cameos.

The Marvel Cinematic Universe newcomer tried his best not to play coy during a conversation with Rolling Stone . When pressed on whether comic book fans will see his shaved head fighting against Robert Downey Jr.'s Doctor Doom at any point in the next year or so, he insisted he doesn't have any additional team-up movies on his plate for now.

"I don't think so," when asked if he'll appear in any cameo roles before X-Men. "I don't even know… See, what's happening? What do you mean?"

Christopher Abbott, who will play Professor X in 2028's ‘X-Men’ reboot, says he will not be in the upcoming Avengers movie. “I don't think so. Well, I don't even know–what's happening? What do you mean? I don't know what's going on. On no. I'm not in that. I gotta do the ‘X-Men’ movie first before any of that stuff.” — Rolling Stone (@RollingStone) October 25, 2026

Christopher Abbott, who will play Professor X in 2028's ‘X-Men’ reboot, says he will not be in the upcoming Avengers movie. “I don't think so. Well, I don't even know–what's happening? What do you mean? I don't know what's going on. On no. I'm not in that. I gotta do the ‘X-Men’ movie first before any of that stuff.”

When the interviewer clarified, asking if he'll play in Doomsday, he had a quick reply: "No, I'm not in that."

Abbott joined a cast of other would-be mutant heroes when Marvel Studios confirmed he had been picked to play Professor X at D23 earlier this year. The announcement also came with a May 2028 release date, giving him plenty of time to prepare to play the group's leader, and if fans are lucky, show up for a scene or two beforehand.

After all, Doomsday and Secret Wars aren't just your run-of-the-mill superhero flicks. These are saga-ending event films packed to the gills with A-listers and, of course, cameos to keep the MCU going well into the future. With the 2000s versions of the X-Men, including Patrick Stewart's version of Charles Xavier, having already shown up for a few Doomsday trailers, many have wondered if the new X-Men cast would show up on-screen before Marvel's 2027 slate launched. If Abbott is out, though, the chances of an early MCU debut for other X-Men (besides Sadie Sink's Jean Grey ) just got a little less likely.

"I gotta do the X-Men movie first before any of that stuff," he continued.

When the interviewer interjected, pointing out that hard launching characters without a cameo is "famously not how Marvel works," Abbott said with a chuckle, "Look, no coyness: I'm not in that movie."

With Doomsday less than two months from its December 18, 2026, release date, it really does sound like Abbott won't show up. However, his answer regarding Secret Wars, the only other movie between now and X-Men, didn't seem quite as definitive. With more than a full year before that film follows come December 17, 2027, and no trailers out yet, who knows? That said, at least as far as this new take on Professor X is concerned, it is still probably best not to get hopes up too high in the meantime.

Set to join Abbott on the team are Inde Navarrette as Rogue, Maya Boyd as Storm, Asa Germann as Angel , and more. We'll at least see the X-Men team unite when the reboot premieres May 5, 2028. Until then, you can get a sneak peek at Navarrette's progress on developing Rogue's accent .
