articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Review: An Unbelievably Smooth Action Game Filled With Memorable Boss Fights, Compelling Combat, and Limitless Swagger
articles.summary: Memorable boss fights, compelling combat, and limitless swagger.
articles.body:
Phantom Blade Zero has spent years looking almost too good to be true, especially coming from a studio that's best known for its mobile games. That’s why it's just about the biggest compliment I can pay it that after 50 hours performing picture-perfect kung fu, it's exactly as fun to play as it looks. This effortlessly smooth action game has some of the most satisfying and well-tuned combat I’ve played in a long time, a surprising number of secrets to discover and quests to complete in each of its beautiful levels, and a neverending supply of clever encounters full of unbelievably awesome moments. Its convoluted story and occasional performance issues may not live up to that incredible action, but it nails just about everything else, and there were only a handful of moments where I wasn’t absolutely thrilled to be slicing my way through the ranks of the Wulin.

Phantom Blade Zero plays like something straight out of a wuxia epic. As a metal-as-hell martial artist of mysterious origins with only 66 days left alive to exact your revenge, you set out on an odyssey across the ruined lands of the Phantom World, facing off against all manner of beast and badass along the way. The story here isn’t Phantom Blade Zero’s strong suit as it tries to do a bit too much, shoving in a whole bunch of mystical jargon, dozens of characters, and a needlessly complex timeline, very little of which ultimately pays off anyway. In the first couple hours alone, so much time is spent toggling back and forth between present day, several years ago, several months ago, and several days ago that I was exhausted by all the exposition before I’d even faced my first real boss fight. That said, there are enough likeable characters along the way, especially your unflappable hero named Soul, that I was usually able to forgive it for occasionally wasting my time with unnecessary flashbacks and lengthy explanations.

Besides, you’ll be spending most of your time exploring the world and squaring off against enemies big and small, and it’s pretty clear that Phantom Blade Zero wants you to spend most of your attention on this part of the adventure. And that’s a good thing, too, because by God is it good. It only took a couple minutes for the precise parry and dodge mechanics to feel natural, and the nuanced but not-overly-complex system of weapons, combos, special abilities, and upgrades are rolled out at an extremely smart pace, all of which are easy enough to slip into like a tailored set of flowing wuxia robes. I’m a complete snob when it comes to the feel and pacing of combat in these types of games, so the fact that this immediately felt like reuniting with an old friend made it instantly compelling, and it’s one of those intangible things that’s very hard to get right.

Even more impressive is that not only does the combat feel good right away, it does so across dozens of weapons, each with their own unique moveset. This game that doesn’t just encourage you to change up your weapon loadout at regular intervals, it actually requires you to mix things up since swapping your active melee weapon is one of the ways you can restore your posture meter with a single button press. And since many enemies, particularly bosses, can instantly drain your posture with certain attacks, you’ll be swapping between different options with regularity, forcing you to commit multiple movesets and special abilities to memory. Conveniently, Phantom Blade Zero makes it extremely easy for you to reclaim and reallocate points invested in leveling up weapons, so there’s rarely any reason to stick with a set loadout anyway – especially since you always seem to find the exact tool you need right before entering an area or encountering a boss where it would come in handy. For example, I noticed that I found a water cannon weapon only a few feet away from an area that led to a fire-based boss. Nice.

Beyond that, you’ll unlock a bunch of additional tools like grappling hooks and bows, which have utility both in combat encounters and outside of them since you can use them to reach certain parts of the map or break through barriers that are otherwise impassable. There are also trinkets that offer interesting buffs, like a significant damage increase when you’re at full health, and a skill tree with perks that let you do things like execute a dodge while in mid-air or increase the number of healing items you can carry. There’s a surprising amount of depth to the things you can upgrade and the ways to customize exactly how your Wulin warrior does his thing, and I spent much more time than I typically do in these kinds of games just testing out different weapons and swapping my equipment around as a result. At the very least, it’s worth doing so just to see the unique execution animations when you finish off trash enemies.

You’ll have plenty of time to try them all out as you get your steps in across Phantom Blade Zero’s eight maps, too. Each one is filled with foes to take down, side quests to complete, chests to loot, and secrets to discover. A surprising amount of the places to go and people to meet are completely missable, including the entirety of a very cool questline that sees you getting trained by none other than Donnie Yen as the mysterious gold-masked man (which is actually one of PBZ’s strongest subplots). While most of the side quests are pretty straightforward missions to go somewhere and collect some stuff for a small reward, they gave me more reasons to spend time exploring every nook and cranny, which I was happy to do. And unlike lots of modern games filled with icons on the screen telling you exactly where to go and what to do, Phantom Blade Zero instead makes use of hand-drawn maps that only give you a vague idea of your location in relation to key landmarks, allowing you to explore and fill in the gaps on your own.

If there’s one thing that consistently mucks up this journey, it’s that Phantom Blade Zero suffers from some pretty bad geometry. Soul gets caught on surfaces all the time, and even the tiniest bumps in the road can stop him dead in his tracks, which is pretty hilarious for a guy who can jump 40 feet in the air while doing 19 backflips. Not only that, there are invisible borders all over the place that make exploration janky at times, especially when platforming sections ask you to get to a specific ledge, only for you to discover there’s an invisible wall and you fall to your death. I died nearly 200 times over the course of my playthrough, and roughly half of those deaths were me falling into a pit or getting caught in the environment until I was able to get myself killed or reload my save file. In one case, I even lost about 20 minutes of progress when my supposed martial master couldn’t escape from some bushes. Oh, and enemies occasionally get stuck in the environment too, which just makes fights where it happens feel so lame.

Despite that, Phantom Blade Zero’s superpower – the magic trick it performs time and time again – is its way of making you feel like you’re the only person in the world badass enough to withstand its utterly insane flurry of swords against godlike monsters like it’s nothing. The truth is that the melee dance of combat encounters is just so finely tuned, with every attack telegraphed just enough to give you exactly the time you need to react, aided by an almost imperceptible musical rhythm that grants you a certain level of precognition for what’s going to happen next. Once I synced up with its tempo, I started anticipating attacks before I consciously registered them, leading me to perfectly block some lightning-quick attack I hadn’t seen before. There’s nothing specifically special about my reaction time or skill with action games – rather it's a testament to how incredibly well-balanced and smartly designed these unbelievably sick fights are. It’s without question the thing Phantom Blade Zero does best, and it’s an illusion I fell for repeatedly, from the opening sequence all the way to the final battle.

Something I admire about Phantom Blade Zero’s difficulty is how consistently it feels exactly right – not too unforgiving, but it rarely lets you feel like you aren’t in danger of getting your butt kicked. I’m typically someone who relishes a challenge from games like this and so played Phantom Blade Zero on its hardest difficulty exclusively, but found myself beating just about every major boss fight in two or three tries, plus a good chunk that I cleared in one go – and I didn’t mind that one bit! It meant that I rarely saw enough of a boss to know every tool in their murder belt, and refreshingly made me feel like the one to be feared rather than the other way around. It’s pretty damn cool to enter a room and watch a 10-foot-tall badass with an eight-pack swing around a blade and think, “oh, man. This guy’s totally screwed.”

Part of the way this Goldilocks level of difficulty is achieved is due to the interesting decision to not make you repeat phases of a boss fight that you’ve already cleared. If you get through a first phase that just makes the bad guy mad and then get killed after he turns into an even more hulked-out psycho, you’ll pick back up at the top of that second phase. I’ve been known to get annoyed at having to replay the first phase of a boss fight a dozen times just to get another run at the more challenging part, to the point where multi-phase boss fights in general can get on my nerves these days. By removing this annoyance entirely, it got rid of a lot of potential friction with some of these encounters

It also allows for more freedom in how these encounters are designed, like moments where a boss uses a cheap move that one-shots you instantly if you get hit by it. Normally, including insta-kill moves like that is a good way to send me into a rage, but because my progress was almost never set back far enough to bother getting mad about, I felt a lot more lenient toward that kind of thing. I mean, let’s face it, that crazy attack where you get impaled on a giant spear, then set on fire and smashed face-first into the floor probably should kill you right away, so it’s pretty neat that Phantom Blade Zero found a way to make a devastating moment like that exciting rather than irritating.

It’s also incredibly impressive that throughout the 50 hours it took me to reach credits, as I fought dozens and dozens of bosses, I was continually surprised by the creative enemies it threw at me. Sure, there’s the occasional big-guy-with-a-big-axe or dude-with-sword-you-swear-you-fought-already, but these are by far the exception, not the rule. At one point I found myself wearing a lion dancer mask, jumping around on poles to collect heads of lettuce to power up my fire blast, and in another section I fought a posse of warriors who worked together as one unit to throw preposterously intricate attacks my way – the main threat to my life there was getting caught with my guard down because I was too busy cackling. The boss fights are so consistently interesting, memorable, and numerous that I felt utterly compelled to seek out each and every one of them, which led me to turn this first playthrough into a full-on completionist run to avoid FOMO.

When I previewed Phantom Blade Zero a little over a month ago, one of my primary concerns was how it would perform, and thankfully the version I played for this review had a far more consistent performance. The framerate was much steadier, with only a few times I can recall ever noticing issues during combat. That said, there’s one map in particular where the framerate was consistently pretty terrible, specifically on a part of the map where something seems to not be working right. This feels like the type of thing that could pretty easily be identified and fixed, so I’d be surprised if a patch doesn’t arrive at or shortly after launch, but it’s worth shouting out since I suspect there are other lingering issues hiding about.

articles.title: Mass Effect's Commander Shepard Actors, Destiny Community Help #SaveMassEffect Petition Cross 200,000 Signatures
articles.summary: The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.
articles.body:
The #SaveMassEffect movement has picked up even more steam after videos from both Commander Shepard actors – and even posts from the Destiny community – helped its petition reach 200,000 signatures.

It's been a whirlwind week for Mass Effect players and fans of the now-shuttered legendary RPG developer BioWare. After EA announced it would be closing the studio and canceling development for Mass Effect 5 , fans took action , and the result is something to behold.

In the first weekend of the #SaveMassEffect movement and its accompanying petition, more than 200,000 verified users have offered their signature to the cause. That's thanks in part to the wild amount of social media attention it's garnered in just a few days, but two of its most prominent supporters have already been backing Mass Effect for decades.

I like this thought… ❤️💙 #MassEffect #Femshep #broshep #N7 — Jennifer Hale (@jhaletweets) October 24, 2026

I like this thought… ❤️💙 #MassEffect #Femshep #broshep #N7

"You know what I like to think about?" actor Jennifer Hale, who famously played the female version of Commander Shepard for the first three Mass Effect games, said in a video over the weekend. "I like to think about a world where the fans come together to create a Kickstarter, and then a couple of investors join them, and then a really cool game company joins them. Then a collective is formed to bring Mass Effect back to life for the community, for the creatives – for all of us – and it's amazing. That's what I like to think about."

It's a scenario that fans have pushed for, and one Hale believes in. She had already spoken out about the sadness surrounding BioWare's closure after a leaked trailer for its canceled Mass Effect: Universe project found its way online. At the time, she felt "weirdly hopeful," and just a few days later, she donned the #SaveMassEffect hashtag in a post .

When Hale first shared her feelings about EA's decision to lay off staff and bring the game side of the franchise to a halt , she wasn't alone. Joining her during an Instagram livestream was male Shepard actor Mark Meer. He echoed her thoughts, saying that it was "very sad news" for BioWare's home location in Edmonton, Alberta, Canada, and the industry as a whole. He returned to social media to share a similar video , #SaveMassEffect in tow.

I like it too. Hold the line. #MassEffect #SaveMassEffect #N7 #MassEffectIsAlive #CommanderShepard — Mark Meer (@Mark_Meer) October 24, 2026

I like it too. Hold the line. #MassEffect #SaveMassEffect #N7 #MassEffectIsAlive #CommanderShepard

"I just saw my friend, Jennifer Hale, post about an idea, and I think it's a pretty good one," Meer said. "Save Mass Effect. Hold the line. I should go, and you should go… sign that petition."

At the time of this story's publication, the #SaveMassEffect petition on Change.org, which aims to "prominently illustrate to EA the significance of this iconic series" and demand it continue, has crossed the 200,000-signature mark. It's thanks in part to the continued signal boosting from notable figures like Hale and Meer, who may not have even been included in new Mass Effect games, but they aren't the only ones without a stake in the franchise's future who chose to speak up.

Destiny players, who did their own fair share of organizing when Sony moved to cease development of Destiny 2 content earlier this year, have been a vocal force in the aftermath of BioWare's closure. Although it's hard to say whether organization of this magnitude might impact any decisions to give BioWare developers and their ideas a path forward, the effort is a bit heartwarming to see.

Others from different gaming communities have also done their best to lend a hand. You don't have to search too hard to find posts encouraging anyone who's ever had a brush with Shepard's fight against the Reapers to lend their signature to the cause. Another significant helping hand arrived from developer Owlcat Games, which used the official X/Twitter account for its upcoming game, The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, to ask followers to consider signing the petition in a currently pinned post .

#SaveMassEffect — Guardians For Destiny 3 📀 (@GuardiansForD3) October 24, 2026

The Expanse show was saved by fans in the past. So the #SaveMassEffect movement has our full support. Please consider signing the petition (link in the quoted post). — The Expanse: Osiris Reborn (@TheExpanseRPG) October 25, 2026

The Expanse show was saved by fans in the past. So the #SaveMassEffect movement has our full support. Please consider signing the petition (link in the quoted post).

Posts from the destiny community on Reddit

Don’t forget, Guardians. We share a bond with Mass Effect. Do your part. #SaveMassEffect — Jessie Yun (@JessieYun4music) October 24, 2026

Don’t forget, Guardians. We share a bond with Mass Effect. Do your part. #SaveMassEffect

Last month, Destiny players were shocked to hear that Bungie was revisiting its plans for the franchise after its community spoke up . In general, revivals at this level are unlikely, and there's no telling if Mass Effect fans will be quite as lucky, but for now, fans don't seem to show any sign of stopping. While we wait to see what is, hopefully, next for the legendary sci-fi RPG series, you can learn more about Mass Effect: Universe thanks to some recently leaked gameplay details . You can also read about the fans hoping to organize a boycott against EA .

articles.title: Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 Gets Surprise 10th Anniversary Update This Week
articles.summary: Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment.
articles.body:
Bandai Namco has revealed a 10th anniversary update for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 as fans await the fighting game series' third installment .

The publisher detailed the contents set to drop in the coming days on its website . Split between two major releases – one October 27, the other October 30 – all the new goodies will be available for anyone who has picked up Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 on PC, PlayStation 4, PlayStation 5, Xbox One, or Xbox Series X/S since it first launched October 25, 2016.

The first free update is said to bring login bonus rewards, special costumes, and an update for the Future Saga Chapter 4 DLC's Gallery of Time when it launches Tuesday. A true birthday celebration, called "Final Festival of Universes," will follow with hard-to-find items, as well as unlocks for Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 rewards, come Friday.

"During the Final Festival of Universes, you will be able to raise your camaraderie level with characters who have accompanied you on your journey, choosing between Trunks, The Supreme Kai of Time, or Fu," according to an official description. "Doing so will unlock special illustrations. In addition, hard-to-obtain items will be coming back, and you will be able to earn 25 times more Star Coins than usual, making it easier than ever to exchange them for rewards."

Today marks 10 years since Bandai Namco launched its Dragon Ball action RPG follow-up. The Final Festival of Universes seems to be the publisher's sendoff for the sequel, which makes sense considering there's another game right around the corner.

Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was re-revealed for PC and consoles in April of this year and promised to drop players into West City in Age 1000. In an official description shared at the time, Bandai Namco said, "The game combines an epic story-driven RPG experience that will take DRAGON BALL fans on an unforgettable, action-packed journey into this new universe and its cast of characters."

Fans were hoping the 10-year wait for a third installment wouldn't be too much longer when Dragon Ball Xenoverse 3 was first revealed with its broad 2027 release date. Unfortunately, following narrowed release plans shared earlier this month, it's looking like we'll have to wait another year to go hands-on. When updates will arrive before then is unclear, with producer Masayuki Hirano attributing the slight push back to a desire to "fully realize our ambitions for both the launch experience and the content we plan to operate and support afterward."

The Dragon Ball Xenoverse 2 festivities should help the more impatient fans for at least a little while longer. In the meantime, you can read IGN's original 7.5/10 review for the sequel, where we called it "an ambitious, if rough-edged experience, with deceptively deep RPG and brawling elements."

articles.title: Eric Bauza, Voice Acting Legend Behind Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, Dead at 46
articles.summary: Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.
articles.body:
Eric Bauza, the voice acting legend behind Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, and countless other classic characters, has died at 46.

Confirmation of Bauza's passing arrived in a post shared on his Instagram account . As reported by KTLA , the Los Angeles County Medical Examiner's Office said he died October 25, 2026, of hypertensive cardiovascular disease.

Additional details surrounding the sudden announcement remain unclear. His family promised to share more soon with a message posted on social media.

"Eric Bauza, Emmy Award-winning voice actor and the modern voice of iconic Looney Tunes characters Bugs Bunny and Daffy Duck, along with dozens of other beloved cartoon characters, has passed away suddenly," a message from his family said. "More details to come."

Bauza has such a thorough career in animation and voice acting that almost everyone who has enjoyed any TV shows, movies, or games in the last 25 years has probably heard his work. His time lending his unforgettable talent in the industry started with smaller roles in the 2000s, including spots in World of Warcraft, El Tigre: The Adventures of Manny Rivera, Avatar: The Last Airbender, The Sims 2, Chowder, and Alvin and the Chipmunks: The Squeakquel, just to name a few, but it wasn't long before he graduated to become the prolific actor he's known as today.

In the 2010s, Bauza took on parts in video games like Batman: Arkham City, Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance, and Lightning Returns: Final Fantasy 13. Eventually, his work in animation took him to the Looney Tunes universe, where he would go on to play modern iterations on characters like Bugs Bunny, Daffy Duck, Elmer Fudd, Marvin the Martian, and many, many others.

"I’m in complete shock and disbelief," Phineas and Ferb's Vincent Martella said. "A tremendously talented and kind coworker who I always had great conversations with and learned from. Sending so much love to his family. He was a giant. A titan in our industry."

More recently, pop-culture fans may have caught him voicing a few names in Invincible or The Super Mario Galaxy Movie. He also played characters in kids-programming-turned-horror-film Buddy, as well as High on Life 2. Moviegoers heard him reprise his role as Bugs Bunny and other classic Looney Tunes characters in the once-shelved Coyote vs. Acme when it made its way to theaters in August of this year. You can also hear him as Jin-Woo, Kuzon, Pich, and more in Avatar: Seven Havens .

For all intents and purposes, Bauza was a legend not just in animation but entertainment in general. You could fill a book just listing the roles he's played, and that's exactly why the internet has already lit up with friends, fans, and fellow entertainers posting their condolences. IGN interviewed Bauza about how he fought to save Coyote vs. Acme in 2024 . You can see some of the ways the internet is remembering the star below.

"I am at a loss for words," Winnie the Pooh actor Jim Cummings shared in a reply to the Instagram post. "Such a young kind man."

"My life was immeasurably changed for the better by having met Eric Bauza," El Tigre creator Jorge R. Gutierrez said. "He just made everything he worked on better. A generational talent. A legend. I would write and design characters giddy thinking how he would bring them to life. And behind the scenes, an incredibly kind, humble and open-hearted good dude. How lucky we all were to have been able to witness his talent shine. And boy did it shine!!! My heart goes out to his family and friends. Adios, amigo. You will never be forgotten."

"I’m so sorry," Ghost of Yōtei star Erika Ishii said. "Much love to you and the rest of the family. He was a good man, a literal voice for change, advocacy, and a pioneer in animation, not to mention the Asian American community. The rest of the voice acting community is here for anything."

articles.title: Xbox Seeks Partner to Support Arkane Lyon as It Finishes Marvel's Blade, Extends Search for Buyer
articles.summary: Microsoft has said it's exploring the possibility of a company coming in to support Arkane Lyon as it works to finish development of Marvel's Blade, and that it's extending the deadline to find a buyer for the studio.
articles.body:
Microsoft has said it's exploring the possibility of a company coming in to support Arkane Lyon as it works to finish development of Marvel's Blade, and that it's extending the deadline to find a buyer for the studio.

Arkane Lyon's 217 employees are currently at risk of losing their jobs unless a buyer is found for the famed immersive sim studio. According to a recent report, Microsoft wanted to close the studio as part of its sweeping cuts in the summer, but French law prevented it from doing so straight away.

Following that report, which claimed Arkane had until November 13 to find a new owner, Microsoft has extended the deadline by a month. Additionally, it said it's looking for a partner to "support" Arkane, presumably with financing, for the final stretch of Marvel’s Blade's development.

Who Is Blade? Marvel’s Vampire Hunter Explained

"We have extended the consultation period by one additional month as we explore options, including finding a partner to support the studio through the development work still ahead," a Microsoft representative told PC Gamer . "This is a defined extension, and we remain committed to keeping the Works Council informed throughout the process."

The studio was first informed of Microsoft’s decision on July 16, shortly after new Xbox CEO Asha Sharma announced similar plans for Compulsion Games, Double Fine Productions, Ninja Theory, and Undead Labs — Ninja Theory was closed while the other studios went independent. Over 1,600 jobs were cut as part of the layoffs across Microsoft's gaming business. More followed, and more are to come.

Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier said he’d be surprised if Arkane Lyon ends up being shut down, however. “Let me share some positive news for a change,” he said on BlueSky . “Despite all the gloomy headlines today, my understanding is that there are multiple paths actively being explored that would save Arkane Lyon.

“Anything can happen during negotiations, but at this point I'd be surprised if the studio is shut down. One important piece of context that many people might not realize: Shutting down a game studio is expensive. Shutting down a French game studio — thanks to labor laws requiring an extended severance period — is VERY expensive. Xbox doesn't want to take on those costs.”

The union is currently pushing for re-employment of affected staff to other studios within Xbox, should Microsoft fail to secure a deal for Arkane Lyon to survive. "The redundancy plan must be adapted to the video game market where, currently, the prospects for returning to work are extremely limited,” said a union rep.

Negotiations are ongoing, but the union hasn’t ruled out seeing Microsoft in court. "Microsoft is looking to divest itself of Arkane, even though the studio is doing well, in order to save money and improve the profitability of its short-term investments," said the rep.

Marvel’s Blade was on track for a reveal early next year and a release in the fourth quarter of 2027, IGN understands. Blade was announced in December 2023 with a reveal trailer, but we've seen nothing of it since. In June, Bethesda Game Studios head Todd Howard was quoted as saying he'd recently seen what Arkane Lyon was cooking up and was impressed . "I'm not at liberty to say when [we'll see more]," Howard teased at the time, "but I saw some stuff just yesterday [on May 21] and the folks at Arkane [Studios, the developers] are doing a really, really great job."

articles.title: Sony Awarded a Hacker $50,000 for Privately Reporting a PS5 Exploit He Found With AI — Now He's Public Enemy Number One
articles.summary: A hacker sparked an uproar within the PlayStation 5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.
articles.body:
A hacker sparked an uproar within the PlayStation 5 homebrew scene for privately reporting an exploit to Sony and cashing in on a $50,000 reward, rather than keeping it confidential for the community.

A hacker who goes by the handle “Jordy” was awarded the bounty from Sony for reporting a vulnerability — found using AI — on the PS5 console. The bug was reported to HackerOne, a site that works with companies to plug issues in their products and services. Essentially, Sony pays hackers to find exploits, then pays them money not to release them until the security hole has been patched.

There wouldn’t normally be anything particularly unusual about a hack being reported to Sony — but in the case of this PS5 exploit, a prominent security engineer discovered it months ago but wanted to hold onto it until GTA 6 launched. Then Jordy discovered it with AI and reported it, triggering the controversy.

In Pictures: How GTA 6's Jason and Lucia Have Evolved Since 2023

The exploit in question is a ‘Hypervisor Bug’ that affects the PS5 on firmware from 13.60 up to 14.00. A hypervisor bug is a fault inside the core software or firmware layer, which allows hackers to execute kernel code to, for example, boot Linux on a machine not designed to do it.

You might have seen a spate of headlines about how AI has fueled an explosion of hacks across the internet. Information security experts are calling this month ‘Black October’ due to several major security incidents and vulnerability disclosures prompted by the growing use of artificial intelligence in research.

Google security engineer Andy Nguyen, aka theflow0, had been working on getting Linux running on PS5 for months. Indeed, back in March, theflow0 showcased the results of his work. But Jordy’s AI-powered bug report put an end to that work. “I am stepping away from the PS5 scene and stopping all my work on PS5 Linux,” he said. “After pouring my heart and months of my life into it, including plans to finish PS5 Pro support and release in 2027, it's all down the sink.

“The scene used to be a group of highly talented researchers, but now it is just a bunch of noobs using LLMs and writing hacks they don't even understand. Slop kiddies found the only hypervisor bug left, which I had also found a while ago, and decided to report to Sony.”

In a conversation with IGN, Jordy admitted using generative AI to find the bug that netted him $50,000. He claimed that theflow0 found the bug back in 2025 but had kept it secret. When Jordy announced he’d found a hypervisor bug himself, theflow0 reached out to see if it was the same one he found the year before. Jordy and theflow0 initially agreed to not report the bug to HackerOne, but another researcher quickly found the same bug shortly after. Jordy made the decision to report the bug as other researchers stumbled on it by using generative AI, closing the window to claim the bounty from Sony.

“I decided I would report it,” Jordy said. “If I and another person can find it with LLM, so can someone else.”

theflow0 couldn’t be reached for comment.

It’s not just the use of AI that made Jordy’s bounty claim controversial. Players who wanted to boot Linux on their consoles are upset because of a certain video game coming out in November. Before the bug was reported, it would have been possible to load Linux onto a PS5 and still run the console through the Sony operating system, which would have allowed people running Linux to play GTA 6 when not using the jailbreak.

“People wanted to buy and play GTA 6 legally on their normal PS5 OS without losing the ability to dual-boot Linux on the same console,” madwax0r, creator of the PS5 emulator tracker and scam blacklist Kaishaku , told IGN. “Think of the PS5 Linux project like turning your console into a high-end Steam Machine that runs off an external USB drive. It's a temporary soft-mod, so whenever you reboot the console, it goes right back to being a normal PS5.

“The catch is that to download and play GTA 6 on November 19, Sony requires you to update to the latest system firmware and sign into PSN. theflow0 wanted researchers to hold off reporting the hypervisor bug until after November 19 so that the launch-day firmware required for GTA 6 would still have the unpatched flaw baked in. That way, players could update their PS5 on launch day, buy GTA 6 legally, and still use the exploit to boot Linux on the same machine.”

Presumably, some would have used the exploit for more nefarious means. There’s sentiment on the internet that Sony “deserved this” because of its policy to end physical discs by 2028. Pirating games — including GTA 6 — is a distinct possibility as those in the homebrew scene continue to point AI at the inner workings of the PS5, with Sony battling to keep up with each potential jailbreak by issuing fresh firmware updates.

Because Jordy — whose mother is terminally ill — reported the bug early, Sony had the chance to patch the exploit ahead of GTA 6’s launch. This leaves modders who want to run Linux stuck with a choice: keep their PS5 offline to run Linux, or update and make the console GTA 6-ready while locking themselves out of Linux.

“What really poured fuel on the fire is the AI angle,” said madwax0r. “Historically, hypervisor bugs were so rare that a researcher could quietly sit on one for a year. Now, with people running console code through LLMs (large language models) to hunt for flaws, multiple people are stumbling onto the same bugs at the same time. Theflow wanted to hold the bug for the community, while Jordy — seeing a third hacker also find it with AI tools, and facing heavy personal pressure with his mother's terminal illness — took the guaranteed $50,000 payout before someone else beat him to it.”

Part of the reason Jordy’s bounty claim went viral was because of his tweet announcing the win. “I can at least buy GTA with this I think,” he said on Twitter , along with a screenshot of the payout. At the time of writing, the tweet had 1.8 million views. IGN asked Jordy if he thought the tweet might have been what antagonized the audience. “Probably but that was the point,” he replied. “I’m nearly 30 years old. I could care less about people not being able to pirate a game, let alone do I want to enable modding it.”

Because of the timing of the bounty claim, some of the audience also believe Jordy was coached on how to find the bug by theflow0, which is another reason people are angry. The researcher denies this and claims he found it independently. “Yes, with AI,” he said. “A lot of people want to downplay that but nobody else is finding bugs like that.” Jordy added that theflow0 is “a legend” and a respectable figure in the industry.

Since he announced he had received the $50,000 bounty, Jordy has faced repeated criticism on social media from those in the scene who believe he should have held off. “50k in bank but 0 friends left. Worth it?” one person asked. “You're insane to think I lost friends over reporting a bug I found myself, even flow who isn't happy with my choice I can still contact privately,” Jordy replied. “You guys act like I'm a domestic terrorist or something?”

Some, though, have supported Jordy cashing in on the bounty. “$50k pays the bills, your opinion doesn’t,” one person said in response to a critic. “You also would report bug to get 50k, like that’s a life changing amount of money for a lot of people,” another added. “He got paid 50k$ idiot! What did u think that he was gonna do, turn it down so you could play GTA 6 on a Nintendo DS?” commented another.

Last week, Sony issued a new PS5 firmware update that some believe was designed to combat the homebrew community's ongoing effort to jailbreak the console . There is a game of Whac-A-Mole at play where the homebrew scene is working to release a new jailbreak for the latest PS5 firmware, then do it all over again when Sony releases a new firmware update designed to beef up security. This in turn has sparked concern that if a PS5 jailbreak is made available for the firmware that is required by GTA 6, which comes out in less than a month, then it may be possible for Rockstar’s game to be pirated on PS5 and maybe even made available on PC.

Jordy also claimed that this won’t be the last hypervisor bug people find on PS5. Cybersecurity researcher Eric Parker agreed. “I imagine there will probably be another exploit at some point,” he said. If Jordy’s claims are true, it might not be the last hypervisor bug on PS5, which means hackers could find a way around the 14.00 patch in the future. Linux is already up and running on pre-patch PS5s .

The question for Sony is whether it can do enough to eventually win this game of Whac-A-Mole with the homebrew scene. This is something of an existential crisis for Sony, which publishers and developers rely upon for the security of their PlayStation releases. But with the emergence of powerful AI models, the stakes have risen significantly.

For Jordy, the money represents time — time he can spend with his family and looking after his sick mother. “I will continue to research,” he said. “Just really no time lately.”

articles.title: 'Treehouse of Horror XXXVII' Isn't Half-Bad, but It's Not the Best Halloween Special in The Simpsons' 38th Season
articles.summary: "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII" is far from the worst Halloween special The Simpsons has delivered, but it can't compare to Season 38's other Halloween episode.
articles.body:
Full spoilers follow for The Simpsons : "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII."

While it's best to go into modern "Treehouse of Horror" episodes with tempered expectations, the truth is that The Simpsons' track record with Halloween specials has improved a fair bit in recent years. "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII" is far from the strongest the series has ever delivered, but nor is it anywhere near the weakest. Its main flaw is in being a just plain decent episode in the immediate aftermath of the much superior "Treehouse of Horror Presents: The Revengening."

Unlike last week's special, which focused on one singular storyline involving Homer (Dan Castellaneta) and his compatriots being hounded by a bloodthirsty slasher villain with a surprising secret identity , this episode reverts to the traditional "Treehouse" formula. That means a cleverly animated intro sequence (in this case, a neat little claymation parody of The Nightmare Before Christmas) followed by three spooky shorts. My main takeaway from watching these two episodes back-to-back is that the series really ought to consider switching to the full-length episode format more permanently. But if the plan is to start doing both every year, then who are we to complain, really?

The Simpsons: Every Treehouse of Horror Episode Ranked

If there's no one particular standout segment in this year's "Treehouse," at least there aren't any weak links, either. The episode opens with the cleverly titled "Bride's Shed Revisited," as Marge (Julie Kavner) assembles a backyard shed that winds up switching out husbands at random. It's amusing to watch Marge lean into her dubious new power and cycle through the best and worst eligible mates Springfield has to offer, culminating in Survivor host Jeff Probst. I can even forgive the idea of Marge hooking up with Probst, since this episode is (as Lisa reminds us in the intro) strictly non-canon.

That's followed by "Dog Boy Afternoon," a very loose Pet Sematary parody that sees Homer accidentally kill both Santa's Little Helper and Bart (Nancy Cartwright) and inadvertantly cause their corpses to switch brains. It's a fun little segment that benefits both from the recurring gag of Homer drinking his way through morning and afternoon-themed liquor and the general body-swap comedy. There's also a surprising amount of gore here, particularly in the scene where Homer is ripped apart by hungry dogs. It's always nice to see these Halloween specials push the envelope in that regard.

Finally, there's "Vehicular Dad Slaughter," as teen versions of Bart and Lisa (Yeardley Smith) discover their dear old dad has been imprisoned in DMV training video limbo by Patty and Selma (Kavner). I like that writer Tim Long opted to jump forward in time for this segment, even if the segment could just as easily have been executed with the traditional characters. Patty and Selma also make for solid witchy antagonists here.

If there are any unifying themes to this year's special, it's the emphasis on exploring the Simpsons clan at different eras of their lives and in spotlighting Kavner's characters over the rest of the ensemble cast. Both work to the episode's benefit. The focus on Marge and her sisters might have given me pause in seasons past, as Kavner's voice has deteriorated quite a bit over the years (granted, the same could be said for several cast members of this nearly 40-year-old sitcom). But whether through some sort of digital AI assistance or just plain effort on her part, that's another area the series has improved upon of late. Kavner's Marge sounds closer to her old self these days.

Again, none of these three segments are good enough to rival the all-time "Treehouse of Horror" classics, but nor are there any stinkers this time. That's still only enough to make "Treehouse of Horror XXXVII" the second-best Halloween episode of Season 38.

articles.title: Horror Games Are Getting Big Discounts in the Lead-Up to Halloween
articles.summary: Save on Resident Evil, Silent Hill, and many more horror games in this sale at Amazon and Best Buy.
articles.body:
I don’t know if you’ve looked at a calendar lately, but Halloween is coming up. To celebrate the spookiest of holidays, Best Buy is running a sale on horror games. And as often happens, Amazon is price matching many of the deals. So if you could use a dose of horror in your gaming life, now is an excellent time to pick up a game like Resident Evil Requiem, Silent Hill 2, Alan Wake 2, and more. Let’s dive in.

Pretty much any AAA horror game you’d want to play from recent years is on sale right now. We’ve got several Resident Evil remakes (2 and 3 specifically), as well as this year’s all-new entry Resident Evil Requiem on sale. Silent Hill fans can pick up the excellent remake of Silent Hill 2 for $22.99, or last year’s Silent Hill f for $29.99.

There’s a good chance you’ve already played the fungal zombie games The Last of Us Part I and The Last of Us Part II, but if you don’t have the most recent PS5 releases, now is a good time to add them to your collection since they’re $29.99 each. Death Stranding 2 is creepy, and so it’s on sale for $39.99. Until Dawn is basically an interactive horror movie that’s great to play either alone or with a group. The PS5 version is on sale for $29.99.

Alan Wake II is a gritty detective game that’s equal parts Se7en and Twin Peaks. It’s on sale for $29.99. Those who enjoy a good asymmetrical online multiplayer game can pick up the brand-new Halloween: The Game for $34.99.

Rounding out the sale are a Goosebumps game, as well as Little Nightmares 3 and Cult of the Lamb. Oh, and if you want a creepy take on Pac-Man (and who doesn’t?) you can pick up Shadow Labyrinth for just $14.99.

In related news, Best Buy has kicked off the Best Buy Gamers program , which offers info about sales and upcoming games. If you sign up (for free), you get a free $5 credit.

Chris Reed is a senior commerce editor and deals expert for IGN. He also runs IGN's LEGO coverage and maintains the upcoming release dates articles for video games , LEGO sets , and 4K Blu-rays . You can follow him on Bluesky .
